wood.name: Wood
wood.desc: Logs from felled trees. Builders and households always need it — especially in winter.

stone.name: Stone
stone.desc: Rough stone from rocks and the quarry.

iron_ore.name: Iron Ore
iron_ore.desc: Rusty-red ore. The blacksmith turns it into tools.

coal.name: Coal
coal.desc: Black fuel that keeps the forge hot.

wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.desc: Golden grain. The store bakes it into bread.

berries.name: Berries
berries.desc: Wild berries from forest bushes. Free food, if not very filling.

apple.name: Apple
apple.desc: A crisp apple brought in by traders.

bread.name: Bread
bread.desc: A fresh loaf. Cheap and filling.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.desc: A wedge of aged cheese. Filling and good for you.

pie.name: Berry Pie
pie.desc: Baked at the tavern. Restores a little energy too.

stew.name: Hot Stew
stew.desc: A hearty tavern meal. Very filling and warming.

worn_axe.name: Worn Axe
worn_axe.desc: Your old axe. Dull and chipped, but it still cuts.

axe.name: Axe
axe.desc: A sharp axe from the smithy. Chops faster and lasts longer.

pickaxe.name: Pickaxe
pickaxe.desc: Needed to break rocks and mine ore.

package.name: Package
package.desc: A parcel from the store. Deliver it to the right house.

clay.name: Clay
clay.desc: Soft river clay. Fired into bricks.

planks.name: Planks
planks.desc: Sawn boards. Used for furniture and buildings.

bricks.name: Bricks
bricks.desc: Fired clay bricks for sturdy buildings.

pumpkin.name: Pumpkin
pumpkin.desc: A heavy autumn pumpkin. Very filling.

vegetable_soup.name: Vegetable Soup
vegetable_soup.desc: Hearty home-cooked soup. Restores energy and health.

wheat_seeds.name: Wheat Seeds
wheat_seeds.desc: Plant on tilled soil. Grows in spring and summer.

carrot_seeds.name: Carrot Seeds
carrot_seeds.desc: Plant on tilled soil. Quick to grow.

potato_seeds.name: Potato Seeds
potato_seeds.desc: Plant on tilled soil. Reliable yield.

cabbage_seeds.name: Cabbage Seeds
cabbage_seeds.desc: Plant on tilled soil. Slow, but valuable.

pumpkin_seeds.name: Pumpkin Seeds
pumpkin_seeds.desc: Plant on tilled soil. Grows in summer and autumn.

stool.name: Stool
stool.desc: A simple wooden stool. Keep it at home for comfort, or sell it.

chair.name: Chair
chair.desc: A sturdy chair. Villagers with money like to buy these.

table.name: Table
table.desc: A handsome dining table. Valuable furniture.

iron_axe.name: Iron Axe
iron_axe.desc: A heavy iron axe. Much faster and very durable.

iron_pickaxe.name: Iron Pickaxe
iron_pickaxe.desc: A heavy iron pickaxe. Much faster and very durable.

saw.name: Saw
saw.desc: Needed to make furniture. Speeds up carpentry.

hoe.name: Hoe
hoe.desc: Needed to till soil for planting.

watering_can.name: Watering Can
watering_can.desc: Water your crops. Refill at a well or the river.

fish.name: Fish
fish.desc: Fresh from the water. Better grilled.

grilled_fish.name: Grilled fish
grilled_fish.desc: Crispy skin, flaky flesh. A proper meal.

meat.name: Game meat
meat.desc: From the hunt. Cook it before eating.

hide.name: Deer hide
hide.desc: Tanners and shops pay for good hides.

fishing_rod.name: Fishing rod
fishing_rod.desc: Stand at the water's edge and press E to fish.

bow.name: Hunting bow
bow.desc: Hunt deer and rabbits in the woods. They bolt if you come too close — stand still.

relic.name: Ancient relic
relic.desc: A bronze amulet from the old fort's time. Worth a lot to the right buyer — and full of history.

iron_ingot.name: Iron ingot
iron_ingot.desc: Smelted from iron ore and coal at a forge. Tools and fittings are made from it.

cabinet.name: Cabinet
cabinet.desc: A tall cabinet with iron fittings. Very comfortable to own — and valuable.

flour.name: Flour
flour.desc: Wheat ground at the mill. Bakers make twice the bread from it than from grinding wheat by hand.

gemstone.name: Gemstone
gemstone.desc: A clear blue stone from deep in a cave. Traders pay well for it.

glass.name: Glass
glass.desc: Window panes, brought in from the towns. Better houses need them.

egg.name: Egg
egg.desc: A fresh egg from your hens. Three make an omelette at the stove.

milk.name: Milk
milk.desc: A pail of milk from your cows. Three make a cheese at the stove; the store buys it too.

wool.name: Wool
wool.desc: A fleece shorn from your sheep. The store buys it.

hay.name: Hay
hay.desc: Winter fodder for animals. The farm cuts it in summer; the store sells it.

omelette.name: Omelette
omelette.desc: Three eggs in a hot pan. Quick and filling.

woodcutting.name: Woodcutting
woodcutting.desc: Chop trees faster; every 3 levels gives +1 wood per tree.

mining.name: Mining
mining.desc: Mine faster. Coal needs level 1, iron needs level 2.

foraging.name: Foraging
foraging.desc: Gather berries faster; every 2 levels gives +1 berry.

farming.name: Farming
farming.desc: Harvest faster, with a chance of extra wheat.

trading.name: Trading
trading.desc: Better prices when buying and selling (+2% per level).

negotiation.name: Negotiation
negotiation.desc: Employers pay you more (+4% per level).

smithing.name: Smithing
smithing.desc: Smelt iron and forge tools at a forge; finer tools as you improve. Cheaper repairs (−8% per level).

learning.name: Learning
learning.desc: Gain more XP and skill XP from everything (+5% per level).

construction.name: Construction
construction.desc: Build faster (+8% per level). Needed for bigger buildings.

carpentry.name: Carpentry
carpentry.desc: Craft planks and furniture faster; unlocks better furniture.

leadership.name: Leadership
leadership.desc: Manage more workers; your whole team works better.

fishing.name: Fishing
fishing.desc: Fish bite more often for you, and you fish faster.

hunting.name: Hunting
hunting.desc: Your arrows find their mark more often.

cooking.name: Cooking
cooking.desc: Cook at a stove: better meals that restore more and sell for more. More recipes as you improve.

exploration.name: Exploration
exploration.desc: Safer expeditions that map more and find more. Improves on the road and walking unknown country.

strength.name: Strength
strength.desc: +5 kg carrying capacity; chop and mine faster.

agility.name: Agility
agility.desc: Walk faster; work a little faster.

charisma.name: Charisma
charisma.desc: Relationships grow faster; slightly higher pay.

craftsmanship.name: Craftsmanship
craftsmanship.desc: Better shift work pay; chance of extra harvest.

leadership.name: Leadership
leadership.desc: Reputation grows faster. Later: manage workers.

farm_harvest.name: Harvest help
farm_harvest.desc: Farmer Gregory needs hands. Harvest ripe wheat from the fields and bring it to the farmhouse.

lumber_delivery.name: Wood delivery
lumber_delivery.desc: The lumberyard is behind on orders. Chop wood and bring it to the yard.

courier.name: Courier run
courier.desc: Pick up a package at the store and deliver it to a villager's home.

dishwasher.name: Evening dishwashing
dishwasher.desc: The tavern gets busy in the evening. Wash dishes for a few hours.

store_assistant.name: Store assistant
store_assistant.desc: Help Vera stock shelves and serve customers. You'll learn a lot about trading.

quarry_miner.name: Quarry work
quarry_miner.desc: Break stone for the quarry. Bring your own pickaxe.

smith_apprentice.name: Smith's apprentice
smith_apprentice.desc: Work the bellows and swing the hammer at the forge. Hard work, good pay.

farm_chores.name: Morning chores at the farm
farm_chores.desc: Feed the animals, muck out, carry water. An early start.

spring_planting.name: Spring planting
spring_planting.desc: Help the farmer sow the fields while the ground is soft.

firewood.name: Firewood for the tavern
firewood.desc: The tavern's fires and oven need feeding. Chop wood and bring it in.

tavern_cellar.name: Cellar work
tavern_cellar.desc: Roll barrels, stack crates and sweep out the tavern's cellar.

berry_picking.name: Berry picking
berry_picking.desc: The store sells wild berries. Pick them from the bushes and bring them in.

market_porter.name: Unloading carts
market_porter.desc: Help unload the carts at the store and carry the goods inside.

mail_rounds.name: Letter rounds
mail_rounds.desc: Collect letters at the store and deliver one to each house on the list.

snow_clearing.name: Clearing snow
snow_clearing.desc: Shovel the snow from in front of the shops so customers can get in.

lumber_haul.name: Timber haul
lumber_haul.desc: Carry a load of timber from the lumberyard to a house being built in the village.

fish_catch.name: Fish for the tavern
fish_catch.desc: The tavern wants fresh fish for tonight's pot. Needs a fishing rod.

tavern_server.name: Evening at the tavern
tavern_server.desc: Serve food and drink on a busy evening. Tips are good if people like you.

stone_haul.name: Stone haul
stone_haul.desc: Carry stone from the quarry to a building site in the village.

bakery_shift.name: Early shift at the bakery
bakery_shift.desc: Knead dough and fire the ovens before dawn. Smells wonderful.

carpenter_helper.name: Carpenter's helper
carpenter_helper.desc: Saw, plane and hold things steady in the carpenter's workshop.

warehouse_loader.name: Warehouse loader
warehouse_loader.desc: Load and unload the carts and caravans at the warehouse.

fishery_crew.name: Fishing crew
fishery_crew.desc: Fish for the fishery and bring in the catch. Needs a fishing rod.

hunt_meat.name: Game for the tavern
hunt_meat.desc: Hunt deer or rabbits and bring the meat to the tavern. Needs a bow.

mill_hand.name: Mill hand
mill_hand.desc: Heave sacks of grain and flour at the mill. Hard, honest work.

titlescreen.subtitle: Life · Settlement · City · Civilization
titlescreen.intro: You arrive in a small river village with $25, a worn axe and two loaves of bread. You rent a leaky shack by the river. Everything else is up to you.
titlescreen.footer: WASD to move · E to interact · Esc for the menu

ui.inventory_hint: Tip: press Q anywhere to eat the most suitable food.
ui.skills_hint: Skills improve with practice. Skill points raise a skill instantly.
ui.nothing_to_sell: You have nothing this shop wants.
ui.shop_hint: Prices change with supply and demand: buying raises them, selling lowers them.
ui.request_rumor: {npc} is looking for {item} ×{qty}. Talk to them.
ui.jobs_hint: Jobs refresh every morning. What's offered depends on the season and how the businesses are doing.
ui.no_job: You have no job right now. Check the notice board on the plaza.
ui.news_hint: Everything here happened on its own — the village lives whether you watch or not.
ui.quit_hint: Unsaved progress since your last sleep or save will be lost.
ui.save_hint: The game also autosaves every time you sleep.
ui.language_hint: The language switches instantly — no restart needed.
ui.inspect_hint: Villagers improve with experience: apprentice → regular → skilled (level {r}) → master.
ui.storage_hint: Furniture kept at home makes it cozier. Home comfort: {comfort} (better sleep).
ui.craft_hint: Materials are taken from your pockets first, then from your chest.
ui.land_hint: Trees you cut on your own land don't grow back — clear space to build.
ui.home_shack_hint: You rent this shack. Build a Small House on your land and move in to upgrade it later.
ui.home_max: Your home can't be improved further (yet).
ui.build_hint: Buildings go up in stages: foundation → frame → walls → roof. Deliver materials and work with a hammer — or put workers on it.
ui.your_rate: One hour of your work = {h} h of progress (construction skill, craftsmanship, strength, hammer).
ui.no_builders: Nobody is assigned. Work on it yourself, or assign workers.
ui.cancel_confirm: Cancel construction? Money is not refunded.
ui.site_hint: Work can only get a little ahead of the materials.
ui.road_hint: Click tiles next to a road to extend it (1 stone each) · Right-click / Esc to stop
ui.place_hint: Click on your land to place · Right-click / Esc to cancel
ui.no_workers: No workers yet. Talk to villagers — the unemployed are easiest to hire.
ui.workers_hint: Workers find their own work: the job you give them comes first, and when there is none they help wherever they are needed — fetching or buying missing materials, felling trees, repairing your buildings. They get better at what they do. Pay them well and they work better; ignore them and they quit.
ui.biz_no_workers: Nobody works here yet — assign workers (K) to “Workshop”.
ui.biz_plan_hint: Workers make whatever is furthest below the stock you want to keep.
ui.biz_autobuy: Buy {item} from the lumberyard when low
ui.biz_surplus: Sell surplus to the general store
ui.site_hint_theirs: You can lend a hand (with a hammer) or give materials — they won't forget it.
ui.no_history: Nothing has gone down in history yet.
ui.history_hint: What the village will remember: firsts, milestones, hard times and your family's generations.
ui.village_fund_hint: Rent from village-owned homes pays pensions, poor relief, wells, the teacher — and big projects. You can chip in.
ui.village_saving_for: The village is saving for a {what} (needs {money} to start).
ui.quality_hint: Skill, craftsmanship, a good tool, rest and a little luck decide the quality: crude, standard, fine or masterwork.
ui.craft_hint_forge: At a forge you work with what's in your pockets.
ui.perks_hint: At levels 3 and 7 of a skill you choose one of two perks — the other is gone for good.
ui.taxes_hint: Every week businesses pay {n}% of their profit and owners of bigger properties a small levy. It all goes into the fund.
ui.jobs_available: You can take {n} of {total} jobs right now.

intro: Oh, a new face! I'm {name}, {occ}. Welcome to our village.
Hello there, stranger. Name's {name}. I'm the {occ} around here.
You must be the newcomer everyone's talking about. I'm {name}.
sleepy: *yawn* It's the middle of the night… what do you want?
Mmh… come back in the morning, please.
hungry: Sorry, I can barely think — I haven't eaten all day.
My stomach is growling louder than I can talk.

friend: Hey, {player}! Got a minute to chat?
trusted: {player}! You know my door is always open for you.
My dear friend! What can I do for you?
hostile: I've got nothing to say to you.
You've got some nerve showing your face here.
kin_spouse: Home at last! How was your day?
kin_sibling: Well, if it isn't my own flesh and blood.
kin_child: Look at you — all grown up and still coming to see me.
partner: {player}! I was just thinking about you.

elder: I've watched this village grow for sixty years. It could become something great, you know.
A village needs more than houses. It needs people who care.
child: Wanna race to the well? I always win!
When I grow up I'm going to have the biggest house in the village!
Mum says I can't go into the forest alone. Is it true there are wolves?
unemployed: I've been asking around for work. Nothing yet…
If only someone would give me a chance.
store_clerk: Stacking shelves all day. At least I get to hear all the gossip.
Vera counts every coin twice. I count them three times, just to be safe.
tavern_server: Stew for table three! Oh — sorry, habit.
The evenings are busy, but the tips are decent.
shopkeeper: Business is business — prices go up when stock runs low.
Everyone needs bread. That's why I sell bread.
innkeeper: A warm meal fixes most problems. The rest, a warm bed does.
The tavern is the heart of this village. Everyone ends up here eventually.
farmer: The soil here is good. Give it care and it gives you bread.
Winter's hard on a farm. Nothing grows, but the mouths still need feeding.
farmhand: My back aches, but the fields don't harvest themselves.
Planting, weeding, harvesting… it never ends.
lumber_foreman: Wood is what this village is built on. Literally.
Chop smart, not hard. And never cut the young trees.
woodcutter: Every tree I fell grows back, given time. The forest is patient.
My arms are like iron from all this chopping.
quarry_foreman: Stone lasts forever. Wood rots. Remember that when you build.
There's iron in those mountains. Good money, if you know how to mine it.
miner: The quarry is dusty work, but it pays.
I found a vein of coal yesterday. The blacksmith will be happy.
blacksmith: A good tool is worth ten bad ones.
Bring me iron and coal and I'll forge you anything.
hired_hand: Working for you keeps me busy, that's for sure.
Whatever needs doing, I'll do it.
baker: Up before dawn every day — bread doesn't bake itself.
The smell of fresh bread never gets old.
baker_hand: Kneading dough all morning. My arms are like a blacksmith's!
We start baking at five. The whole street smells of bread.
carpenter: Good timber, sharp tools, steady hands — that's all a carpenter needs.
A well-made chair outlives its maker.
carpenter_hand: I'm learning to make joints that don't need a single nail.
Sawdust everywhere. In my hair, in my boots, in my bread.
smith_hand: I work the bellows and swing the sledge. Hot work.
One day I'll forge my own tools. For now, I hold the tongs.
fisherman: The river gives, if you're patient.
Early mornings on the water — the best time of day.
fisher: Nets to mend, lines to set. A fisher's work never ends.
Some days the nets come up heavy, some days empty.
master_builder: Every house in this village tells me something about its builder.
Measure twice, cut once. And never skimp on the foundations.
builder: Walls up by winter — that's the plan.
My back aches from hauling stone, but look at that roof!
merchant: Buy low from the producers, sell steady to the shops — that's trade.
A full warehouse means nobody goes hungry in a bad month.
warehouse_hand: Sacks in, sacks out. My shoulders know every one of them.
We keep the village's stock. If it's not here, it's not anywhere.
carter_master: Good roads, good carts, and trade flows like a river.
Every rut in these roads costs me a wheel eventually.
carter: From the lumberyard to the store, the quarry to the smithy — I know every road.
The cart creaks, but it carries.
teacher: Some days they hang on every word. Other days I might as well talk to the wall.
When a child finally reads a whole page on their own — that's worth the whole year's pay.
We need more books. Three children to a primer is no way to learn.
doctor: Wash your hands before you eat. I say it to everyone, and I'll keep saying it.
Half of what I learned in town doesn't work here. The other half saves lives.
engineer: That bridge will stand a hundred years if they let me do it properly.
Everything's a sum, in the end. The trick is knowing which one.
researcher: We're close. I can feel it. Another month — if the money holds.
Most days nothing works. Then one day, something does.

sunny: Sun's out — perfect weather for work.
cloudy: Looks like it might rain later.
rain: What a downpour! Good for the crops, at least.
storm: This storm is terrible! Stay indoors if you can.
snow: Snow again… I hope we have enough firewood.
Everything looks so peaceful under the snow.
fog: Can barely see my own hand in this fog.

spring: Spring is when everything starts again.
summer: Long days, warm nights. Summer is the best.
Plenty of work in summer — the fields are busy.
autumn: Harvest season! Busiest time of the year.
Leaves are turning. Winter will be here before we know it.
winter: Winter is long here. Stock up on food and firewood.
No work on the farms now. Times are lean.

price_high: Have you seen the price of {item}? Outrageous.
price_low: {item} is dirt cheap right now — there's plenty of it.
Nobody wants to buy {item} these days, there's too much of it.
poor: Money's tight. I'm counting every coin.
I barely have enough for bread this week.
unpaid: My employer hasn't paid me. How am I supposed to live?
No wages again… I might have to look elsewhere.
empty_pantry: My pantry is empty. I really need to go shopping.
Not a crumb of food at home.

hard_worker: Hard work never killed anyone. Well, almost never.
lazy: Why rush? The work will still be there tomorrow.
I'd rather be napping right now, honestly.
greedy: Everything has a price, friend. Everything.
A coin saved is a coin earned — and two coins are better.
generous: If you ever need anything, just ask.
loyal: I don't abandon people who stand by me.
I've worked in the same place for years. I like it that way.
ambitious: One day I'll have my own business. You'll see.
I won't be a nobody forever.
entrepreneur: This village needs more shops. Someone should open one.
I have so many ideas, I just need the money.
friendly: Isn't it nice to just chat for a bit?
scholar: Did you know the river flows all the way to the sea?
I wish we had a library here.
natural_leader: Someone has to keep this village organised.
People need someone to look up to.
risk_taker: Sometimes you just have to jump.
careful: I like to plan things out properly.

family: {npc} and I are family. We look after each other.
Have you met {npc}? Family means everything to me.
friend: {npc} is my best friend. We talk every evening.

goal.business: I'm saving up. Someday I'll open my own business — just wait.
goal.job: What I need most is steady work.
goal.grow: I want to grow up fast and do grown-up things!
goal.steady: I'm happy with my life. A roof, work, good neighbours.

opt.work: Do you have any work for me?
opt.help: Is there anything I can help you with?
opt.court: Would you like to walk out with me?
opt.back_business: I'll put {money} into your business (for {n}% of it).
opt.offer_house: I have a house to let…
opt.ask_apprentice: Would you take me on as your apprentice ({field})?
opt.offer_apprentice: Would you like to learn {field} from me?
opt.offer_sponsor: I'll pay for your studies in {settlement} ({money})
opt.ask_manager: Would you look after my houses? ({n}% of the rent)
opt.end_manager: You needn't look after my houses any more
opt.job_need: You look busy — could you use a hand?
opt.job_need_note: they have work that needs doing
opt.job_how: About the job I'm doing for you…
opt.job_accept_client: I'll take it on — you buy the materials.
opt.job_accept_included: I'll take it on — give me {money} and I'll get the materials.
opt.job_accept_player: I'll bring the materials myself — pay me {money} for them at the end.
opt.job_ask_pay: Make it {money} and I'll do it.
opt.job_ask_time: I'd need more time than that.
opt.go_work_at: Go and work at {building} for me.
opt.come_back: Come back and work with the rest of the crew.

dialog.no_gifts: You have nothing suitable to give.
chat_again: We already talked today — but I appreciate the company.
Ha, you again! Come back tomorrow for more gossip.
work_hint: I don't hire, but {npc} at the {building} might need help.
Try asking {npc} — the {building} has been busy.
work_none: Honestly, nobody's hiring today. Try tomorrow morning.
Work's scarce today. Check the notice board tomorrow.
request_ask: Actually, yes! Could you bring me {item} ×{qty}? I'll pay you {money}.
I need {item} ×{qty}. I can offer {money} for your trouble.
request_ask_free: Could you bring me {item} ×{qty}? I can't pay much… but I'd be really grateful.
request_done: Exactly what I needed! Thank you so much.
You're a true neighbour. Thank you!
gift_love: {item}? For me? Oh, I love it!
How did you know I love {item}? Thank you!
about_intro: Me? Well, there's not much to tell…
What would you like to know?
hire_ask: Work for you? I'd want {money} a day.
Sure, I could use the work. {money} a day and we have a deal.
hire_employed: I already have a job, you know. It would take a good offer… {money} a day, at least.
hire_yes: You've got yourself a worker. When do I start?
Deal! I won't let you down.
hire_no: I'll have to pass on that.
worker_happy: I like working for you. Fair pay, good boss.
Couldn't ask for a better job!
worker_raise: Honestly? I'd like a raise. Others pay better — {money} a day would be fair.
I've been thinking about my pay… {money} a day would feel right.
worker_unpaid: You haven't paid me! I can't work for nothing.
Where's my money? I have a family to feed.

court_yes.m: I… yes. I was hoping you'd ask, {player}.
court_yes.f: I… yes. I was hoping you'd ask, {player}.

court_yes: Yes! I'd like that very much.
I thought you'd never ask. Yes.
court_no: You're kind, {player}, but… I don't see us that way.
I'm flattered. But no — not now.
propose_yes: {player}… yes. Let's build a life together.
I've been waiting for this. Yes!
propose_no: Not yet, {player}. Give it a little more time.
I care for you — but I'm not ready.
backed_thanks: {money}? You mean it? I'll make it worth your while!
With this I can really do it. You'll get your share, I promise.
stay_yes: …You're right. I'll give it another go.
If you think it's worth staying… all right. I'll stay.
stay_no: I'm sorry. My mind's made up.
It's kind of you. But there's nothing for me here.
let_yes: A house? {building}, for {money} a week? Yes — we'll take it!
You've no idea how long I've been waiting for something like this. We'll move in right away.

too_dear: I'd love to, but I couldn't pay that rent.
That's more than I earn in a week, near enough. Too dear for me.
too_small: It's too small for all of us, I'm afraid.
distrust: Rent from you? After what happened? No, thank you.
not_worth_it: It's not bad, but it's not worth moving for.
happy_here: Thank you, but I'm happy where I am.
owns_home: I've a house of my own, thank you.
not_looking: I'm not looking for a house just now.
no_house: You don't have a house free, do you?

apprentice_yes: All right — come to work when I'm there, and watch what I do. {field} isn't learned in a day.
You want to learn {field}? Then you'll start at the bottom, same as I did.
apprentice_no: I don't know you well enough for that.
Take on an apprentice? Not now, not you.
become_apprentice_yes: Learn {field} from you? Yes! I'll work hard — and {money} a day is fine while I'm learning.
I've been hoping someone would ask. When do I start?
become_apprentice_no: Thank you, but it's not for me.
sponsor_yes: You'd... pay for it? I'll go to {settlement} — and I won't forget this. Ever.
I don't know what to say. Thank you. I'll make it count.
sponsor_no: That's kind, but it's not needed.
manager_yes: Look after your houses? Gladly — I'll see they're let, kept up, and paid for.
For {n}% of the rent? Done. I'll keep an eye on them.
manager_no: I don't think so. I've enough on my plate.
manager_ended: As you like. Your houses were no trouble.
Fair enough. You know where I am.

harvest: There's more wheat ripe in my fields than I can bring in alone — {qty} plants. Could you help me? I'd pay {money}.
My wheat's ready and my back isn't. Would you bring in {qty} plants for me? {money} for the work.
repair: {building} is falling apart — only {n}% sound. Could you put it right? I'd pay {money}.
The roof leaks, the door sticks… {building} needs work. {money} if you'd see to it.
build: My building's going far too slowly. Could you put {hours} hours in on the site? {money} for it.
I could use another pair of hands on the site — {hours} hours. I'd pay {money}.
haul: I'm short of {item}. Could you fetch {qty} from {building} for me? {money} for the carrying.
Would you bring me {qty} × {item} from {building}? I'd pay {money} for your trouble.
water: The sun's baking my wheat — could you water {qty} plants for me? {money} for it.
gather: We're short of {item} at {building}. Could you bring in {qty}? I'd pay {money}.
supply: I'm short of {item}. Could you bring me {qty}? {money} for them.
build_new: You've done good work for me. I'd like a new {vbuilding} built — would you take it on? {money} for the building work.
build_works: You've done good work for me — would you improve {building}? {money} for the work.

job_thanks: Thank you! Will you do it yourself, or send your people?
Wonderful. Who'll be doing the work — you, or your workers?
job_declined: Ah well. Maybe someone else, then.
job_myself: Good. You know where to find me.
Right you are. I'll be glad of the help.
job_crew_sent: Good — I'll show them what's what.
Send them over, I'll be expecting them.
job_crew_none: No one? Then I'm counting on you.
job_progress: Coming along nicely — {what} still to go.
job_not_started: Not a thing done yet. {what} waiting.
job_handed: Thank you — that goes in the barn.
job_all_done: That's the lot! Here's what I owe you.
All in — thank you. Here's your pay.
haggle_yes_pay: You drive a hard bargain. {money}, then.
haggle_yes_time: I suppose it can wait a little. {n} days.
haggle_no_time: I can't wait any longer than that.
No, it has to be done by then.
manage_yes: Me, in charge? I'd be glad to. I'll see everyone's where they should be.
Gladly. I'll keep them all busy — and {money} a day suits me fine.
come_back_yes: Back with the crew — suits me.
I'll come back. Good to be with the others again.

crafting.name: Crafting
crafting.desc: Craft planks and furniture at the workbench in your home.

advanced_gathering.name: Advanced gathering
advanced_gathering.desc: Mine iron ore and work at the quarry.

buy_land.name: Buy land
buy_land.desc: Buy a plot of land of your own.

construction.name: Construction
construction.desc: Build houses, sheds and workshops on your land.

farming.name: Farming
farming.desc: Lay out fields on your land and grow crops.

settlement.name: Found a settlement
settlement.desc: Your land becomes a settlement of its own.

village.name: Village centre
village.desc: expensive, but businesses here get more customers (+25% sales).

water.name: Near water
water.desc: crops grow faster (+25%); you can refill watering cans nearby.

forest.name: Forest
forest.desc: cheap and full of wood, but you have to clear trees before building.

road.name: Road access
road.desc: you and your workers get here quickly.

small_house.name: Small House
small_house.desc: Your own home. Move in and stop paying rent. Can be upgraded later.

rental_house.name: Rental House
rental_house.desc: A house for newcomers. Villagers who move in pay you rent.

storage_shed.name: Storage Shed
storage_shed.desc: +150 kg storage, shared with your home chest. Workers deliver goods here.

well.name: Well
well.desc: Fresh water for drinking and watering crops.

workshop.name: Carpentry Workshop
workshop.desc: Your own business: workers turn wood into planks and furniture that you sell.

road.name: Road
road.desc: Lay roads tile by tile. Everyone walks faster on roads.

forge.name: Forge
forge.desc: Your own forge: smelt iron ingots and make tools without paying the smith.

shopfront.name: Shopfront
shopfront.desc: Premises for a business of your own: a shop, a bakery, a smithy, a workshop…

warehouse_bld.name: Warehouse
warehouse_bld.desc: +400 kg storage for your materials — your workers fetch from here and bring goods back here. It can also be premises for a trading depot.

mining_camp.name: Mining camp
mining_camp.desc: A camp by the rocks: miners work the seams around it for stone, coal and ore — and at a cave, now and then, a gem.

hunting_cabin.name: Hunting cabin
hunting_cabin.desc: Hunters based out in the woods bring in meat and hides (as long as there's game).

trading_post.name: Trading post
trading_post.desc: On the road out of the valley: buys up the village's surplus and sells it to passing traders at good prices.

pave.name: Cobbles
pave.desc: Pave a road with stones: quicker to walk than a dirt road, and the street is worth more to live and trade on.

bridge.name: Bridge
bridge.desc: Planks over shallow water, tile by tile from a road on the bank. Land across the water that a road reaches is worth more.

lamp.name: Street lamp
lamp.desc: A lamp beside a road lights the street at night: people feel safer, and houses near it fetch more.

apartment_house.name: Block of flats
apartment_house.desc: Several households under one roof, each in a flat of its own, each paying its own rent. Flats let for less than a house — for people who can't afford one.

barn.name: Barn
barn.desc: +220 kg storage: grain, feed, tools and timber. Your workers fetch and deliver here.

transport_depot.name: Transport Depot
transport_depot.desc: Parking for your barrows, carts and wagons (+60 kg storage). Equipment is kept and repaired here; level 2 adds a repair bay.

construction_office.name: Construction Office
construction_office.desc: A desk for your contracting: one more contract at a time (two at level 2, three at level 3).

rail_station.name: Railway Station
rail_station.desc: The valley's end of the line: with a station you can lay railways to the towns you trade with (from the journey map). Needs the know-how of railways.

home_tier_desc.house: A proper house: more comfort, a bigger chest, a stove, a second chest. Villagers respect you more.
home_tier_desc.large_house: A large stone house: the best sleep, huge storage, room for a family.

price_level_desc.cheap: Low prices: more customers, less money per sale.
price_level_desc.premium: High prices: more money per sale, but fewer customers.

deflect: I don't know you well enough to talk about that.
That's… personal. Maybe some other time.
nothing: Hm. I don't have much to say today.

player_gave_job: You gave me my chance {ago}, {player}, when nobody else would hire me. I haven't forgotten.
Nobody wanted to hire me — and you did. That was {ago}. I owe you.
player_hired: Leaving my old job for you was a gamble. So far I don't regret it.
Working for you is different. Better, I think.
player_fired: You let me go {ago}. I'm still getting over it.
Oh. It's you. The one who fired me.
player_fired_unfair: I did nothing wrong and you threw me out. I won't forget that, {player}.
Everyone knows how you treated me. Don't expect any favours.
player_raise: Thanks again for the raise. It makes a real difference at home.
The extra coin helps. I noticed, {player}.
player_pay_cut: You cut my pay. Times are hard, I know — but still.
Less money for the same work… it stings.
player_unpaid: I still remember the days you couldn't pay me.
Wages first, {player}. I have to eat too.
player_promoted: You promoted me! I'll prove you were right.
player_loved_gift: That {item} you gave me — I still think about it.
You remembered what I like. That was kind of you.
player_helped: You helped me when I needed it. I won't forget.
Thanks again for the help with the {item}. You're a good neighbour.
player_let_down: You promised to help me and never came back.
I waited for you, {player}. You never showed up.
bought_from_player: That {item} from your workshop is holding up nicely!
Good work on that {item}. Solid craftsmanship.
quit_player: I left your employ {ago}. No hard feelings… mostly.
Working for you just wasn't for me.
heard_player_good: {npc} speaks well of you, you know.
I hear you're someone people can rely on. {npc} says so.
heard_player_bad: People talk, {player}. {npc} has told me how you treat people.
I've heard things about you. Ask what {npc} is saying.
saw_friend_fired: You fired {npc}. {npc} is my friend. I haven't forgotten.
After what you did to {npc}, I'm keeping an eye on you.
player_failed_job: Last time you took a job from me, you didn't finish it.
I hope you'll be more reliable this time.
got_job: I started a new job {ago}! Finally, steady wages.
New job, new life. I'm a {occ} now.
quit_job: I walked out of my job. They stopped paying me.
No wages, no work. I'm done with that place.
unpaid_wages: They haven't paid me at work. I'm getting worried.
Working for free is not what I signed up for.
promoted_rank: Did you hear? I'm a {rank} now!
Years of practice, and now I'm a {rank}.
grew_up: I'm all grown up now. Time to find my own way.
No more children's games for me. I need work.
took_up_hobby: I've taken up {hobby} lately. It clears the head.
My new passion is {hobby}. Don't laugh.
was_sick: I was ill {ago}. Still not quite myself.
Being sick is the worst. I couldn't work for days.
went_hungry: I went to bed hungry {ago}. I don't want that again.
Some days there just isn't enough to eat.
slept_rough: I've been sleeping outside. It's cold, and nobody cares.
No roof over my head. You don't know what that's like.
lived_through: {event}: hard times for all of us.
became_friends: {npc} and I have become good friends lately.
{npc} is great company. We see each other a lot now.
fell_out: I'm not speaking to {npc} any more. Don't ask.
{npc} and I had a serious falling-out.
argued_with: I had words with {npc} the other day. So stubborn!
{npc} just rubs me the wrong way.
fell_in_love: Can I tell you a secret? I think I'm in love with {npc}.
{npc} and I… well. We've been spending a lot of time together.
broke_up: {npc} and I are over. I don't want to talk about it.
married: {npc} and I are married! Best day of my life — {ago}.
Married life suits me. {npc} is wonderful.
family_wedding: There was a wedding in the family! {npc} and {npc2}. Such a party!
child_born: We had a baby! Little {npc}. I haven't slept in days, but I'm so happy.
Have you met {npc}? Our little one. Born {ago}.
sibling_born: I have a new baby {npc} at home! They cry a lot.
family_died: I lost {kin} {ago}. {npc}. Some days I still can't believe it.
Life goes on, they say. It's hard without {npc}.
friend_died: I miss {npc}. We used to talk every evening.
Losing {npc} was hard. A good friend, gone.
inherited: {npc} left me some money. I'd give it all back to have them here.
An inheritance… it doesn't feel like a gift.
took_over_business: I run {building} now. Big shoes to fill.
Taking over {building} was never my plan. But here we are.
retired: I've retired! Now I finally have time for myself.
After all those years of work, I don't quite know what to do with my days.
moved_home: We moved house {ago}. Still getting used to it.
moved_out: I've got a place of my own now! No more sharing a room.
Moving out was scary, but I love my own place.
evicted: They threw me out. I couldn't pay the rent.
bought_home: I bought a house! {building} is mine — nobody can throw me out now.
Years of saving, and now I own my home.
opened_business: I did it — I opened my own {biz_type}! {building}. Come and see!
Being my own boss is terrifying. And wonderful.
family_business: We're running a family business now. It's hard work, but it's ours.
business_struggling: I've put my own savings into the business. I hope it pays off.
Business has been slow. I'm keeping it afloat with my own money.
business_failed: My business failed. Everything I built… gone.
I had to close {building}. I'm starting over.
became_manager: They made me manager! Me, running the place.
Manager now. More pay, more headaches.
laid_off: They let me go. Not enough work, they said.
Laid off. I need to find something new.
changed_jobs: I changed jobs — better pay, better people.
I left my old job. Best decision I ever made.
employee_left: {npc} left me for another job. I trained them, you know.
Good workers are hard to keep. {npc} is gone.
left_player_for_business: I learned a lot working for you, {player}. Now I have my own {biz_type}!
No hard feelings, boss — I had to try running my own place.
backed_business: I've put money into {npc}'s business. I believe in them.
Money should work, not sit in a chest. I backed {npc}.
got_backing: {npc} believed in me and put up the money. I won't let them down.
Without {npc}'s money I'd still be dreaming.
started_building: We're building our own house! Every evening, board by board.
I've started building. It'll take a while, but it'll be ours.
helped_build: {npc} came and helped with the house. That's what neighbours are for.
Couldn't have raised the walls without {npc}.
built_home: We finally moved into the house we built. Every nail in it — ours.
Our own house, built with our own hands. Come and see it!
gave_up_building: I had to stop building. The money ran out before the walls were up.
The half-built house… I just couldn't finish it.
arrived_village: I arrived here with a bag and some hope. Let's see what this place gives me.
Back home there was no work. Here there might be.
friend_left: {npc} left the village. I miss them already.
player_helped_build: You helped raise my house, {player}. I won't forget that.
Every time I look at my roof I think of you swinging that hammer.
home_flood: The flood ruined half our things. Mud everywhere.
We're still drying out after the flood.
home_storm: The storm tore half our roof off.
We lost roof tiles in that storm. Could have been worse.
home_fire: Our house caught fire. We were lucky to get it out.
I still smell the smoke when I close my eyes.
home_burnt: Our home burned down. Everything we had.
We lost the house to the fire. We're starting again.
mine_accident: I was in the quarry when it came down. I'm lucky to be alive.
The collapse… I don't want to talk about it.
took_in: {npc} is staying with us until their house is fixed. That's what neighbours do.
We took {npc} in after the disaster.
fire_helped: {npc} was there with buckets when my house burned. I won't forget it.
When the fire came, {npc} came running.
player_fought_fire: You fought that fire alongside us, {player}. You saved my home.
I saw you with the buckets, {player}. Thank you.
went_exploring: I went all the way to {region_name}, {ago}. You should see it out there.
{region_name} — now that was a journey. My feet still ache.
explored_with_player: Remember our trip to {region_name}? I'd go again, you know.
{region_name}… Those were the days. When's our next trip, {player}?
invented: I figured it out — {tech}! Took me long enough.
People said it couldn't be done. Well: {tech}.
became_teacher: Teaching the children is the best work I've ever done.
The little ones keep me on my toes at school.
mentored_by: {npc} is teaching me the trade. I'm getting better every week.
I learn more from {npc} in a day than I did in a year on my own.
took_apprentice: {npc} works beside me now. Reminds me of myself at that age.
Teaching {npc} the craft — someone has to carry it on.
sold_business_to_player: Selling you the business was the right thing, I think. Look after it.
It's strange, working in the place I used to own. But the burden's off my shoulders.
laid_off_season: The harvest's in, so the farm let me go till spring. Same every year.
No farm work in winter. I'll find something.
goal_achieved: I finally got what I was after. It took long enough!
Remember when it was just a dream? Not any more.
goal_given_up: I had to give up on a dream. Some things aren't meant to be.
moved_near_work: Living near work is a blessing. No more walking half the day.
decided_to_leave: I've made up my mind. I'm leaving.
stayed_for_family: I nearly left, you know. {npc} talked me out of it.
player_backed_dream: You put your money behind my plans. I won't forget that.
When nobody believed in me, you did.
player_asked_stay: You asked me to stay, and I'm glad I did.
I was ready to go. You changed my mind.
player_let_down_backer: I couldn't pay you back in full. I'm sorry about that.
became_headman: Headman! Me! I still can't quite believe it.
Being headman means everyone's troubles land on your doorstep.
bank_loan: The bank lent me the money to start out. Now I have to make it pay.
rented_from_player: Thank you for the house. It's good to have a proper home.
The house you let us suits us fine. Mind the roof in spring, though.
new_interest: I've been getting into {interest} lately. Can't stop thinking about it.
Funny — I never cared for {interest}, and now it's all I want to learn about.
finished_school: I finished school! I can read anything now — well, nearly anything.
They gave me my certificate. Mum cried.
left_school: I stopped going to school. There's work to be done at home.
School wasn't for me. Maybe one day I'll go back.
failed_exam: I failed the exam. I'll have to do the whole year again.
The sums beat me this year. Next year I'll be ready.
finished_course: I finished my course at the trade school! I know what I'm doing now — properly.
A whole year of lessons, and now I've got the papers to show for it.
finished_apprenticeship: My apprenticeship's done. I owe my master everything I know.
They say I'm a journeyman now. Doesn't feel real yet.
apprenticeship_ended: My apprenticeship ended before I'd learned half of it.
No master, no apprenticeship. I'll have to find another way.
wants_retrain: I've been thinking of learning a different trade. This one isn't for me.
Is it too late to start again? I'd like to learn something new.
rose_in_trade: Folk bring their hardest jobs to me now. That's how you know.
Years at the work, and it finally shows.
went_to_university: University! I can hardly believe it.
child_to_university: My child's at the university in town. Imagine that — from our little valley.
The house is quiet without them. But they'll come back a scholar.
graduated: Two years of books and lectures, and now I'm home with a degree.
The town was something. But this is where I'm needed.
failed_degree: I didn't make it through. Maybe it wasn't meant for me.
The exams beat me. I'm not ashamed — I tried.
cant_afford_study: I could have gone to university, if we'd had the money.
They'd have taken me, you know. We just couldn't pay.
took_post: It's a great responsibility. I mean to deserve it.
The whole valley relies on me now. No pressure.
made_discovery: People keep asking me how I thought of it. Honestly, it was years of getting it wrong.
sponsored_by_player: I'd never have got to university without you. Never.
Every lecture I sit through, I think: someone believed in me.
took_player_apprentice: You're coming along. Keep your eyes open and your hands busy.
Most apprentices talk too much. You listen. Good.
taught_player: How's what I taught you coming along?
Come back any time you want another lesson.
player_journeyman: Proud of you. You were a good apprentice.
You learned it properly. That's rare.
improved_building: We finally had the house done up. You wouldn't know it.
Built on at last — there's room to breathe now.
given_notice: You put us out of {building}. We paid every week, you know.
I haven't forgotten the notice you gave us.
rent_raised: The rent's gone up again. Everything costs more these days, I suppose.
{money} a week now for {building}. We'll manage — just.
rent_lowered: Thank you for bringing the rent down. It makes a real difference.
The lower rent — that was decent of you.
manages_player_houses: Your houses are in good hands, don't you worry.
I looked in on your tenants this week. All well.
bought_rental: I've bought {building} to let. The rent will pay for itself in time.
A house to let — that's where money should go, not under the bed.
moved_for: We've moved to {building} — {hwhy}. Best thing we've done in a while.
Have you seen our new place? {building}. We wanted {hwhy}.

owner_struggling: Business is slow. I don't know how long I can keep going.
Money's tight at {building}. Every coin counts.
owner_thriving: Business is good this season. Can't complain!
owner_hiring: I'm looking for another worker, if you know anyone.
I could use another pair of hands at {building}.
owner_no_input: No {item} to work with. My forge is going cold.
If you find any {item}, bring it to me. I'll pay well.
owner_overstock: We've got more {item} than anyone wants to buy.
The yard is overflowing with {item}. Nobody's buying.
player_happy: Working for you suits me fine, boss.
Good pay, a fair boss. I'm happy.
player_ok: The work's fine. Nothing to complain about.
It's a job. I do it.
player_unhappy: Honestly? I think I'm worth more. Something like {money} a day.
I'm not happy with how things are, boss.
unpaid: {npc} hasn't paid me in {n} days. How am I supposed to live?
No wages again. I'm thinking of leaving.
boss_struggling: Things are bad at work. I hope {npc} can keep paying us.
Between you and me, {npc} is short of money.
long_hours: {npc} keeps us working from dawn till dusk.
Long days at work. My back isn't what it used to be.
bad_boss: I can't stand working for {npc} much longer.
good_boss: {npc} is a good boss. Fair and honest.
coworker_friend: Work is easier with {npc} around. We make a good team.
{npc} and I work together. Good friends, too.
proud_master: After all these years, I'm a real master of my trade.
People come to me when something's hard to do. That's what mastery means.
day_off: It's my day off! No work today.
Rest day. I intend to do absolutely nothing.
off_season: No field work until spring. Money's tight.
The off-season is long. I'm just waiting it out.
searching: I've been looking for work everywhere. Nothing yet.
If you hear of a job, tell me, please.
heard_hiring: I heard they're hiring at {building}. I should go and ask.
{building} might need someone. Worth a try.
rival_cheaper: {building} is undercutting me. I'll have to lower my prices.
Customers go where it's cheaper. {building} knows that.
rival_exists: There's competition now — {building}. Keeps me on my toes.
{building} wants my customers. Let them try.
competing_with_you: You make furniture too, don't you? May the better carpenter win!
Your workshop and mine — the village only needs so many chairs.
new_business: It's still early days for my business. Every customer counts.
Opening {building} was the bravest thing I've done.

sick: I'm worried — {kin} is ill. I try to stay close to home.
{npc} hasn't been well for days. I'm worried.
jobless: Still no work for {kin}. It's hard on the whole family.
If you hear of a job, tell {npc} — {kin} really needs one.
child: {npc} is growing up so fast — {n} already!
Kids grow like weeds. {npc} will be working before I know it.
spouse: {npc} and I have been together for years. I'm lucky.
Life's easier with {kin} at my side.
sibling: {npc} always has my back. Family is family.
Family is family — even when {kin} drives me mad.
parent: Everything I know, I learned at home — {kin} taught me.
no_food: Our pantry is empty. I don't know what we'll eat tonight.
Not a crumb at home. Prices are killing us.
courting: I've been seeing {npc}. Don't tell anyone yet!
{npc} and I walk together in the evenings. It's… nice.
widowed: The house is so quiet without {npc}.
crowded: Our house is bursting at the seams. We need a bigger place.
Too many people, too few beds. We have to find something bigger.
rent_behind: I'm behind on the rent. If I don't pay soon, they'll throw me out.
Rent day scares me. I can't pay it all.
your_tenant: The house is fine, landlord. {money} a week is fair.
Renting from you is all right. Just keep the roof fixed!
own_home: It's good to own your home. Nobody can throw you out.
Our home isn't big, but it's ours.

grow: When I grow up, I'll have the biggest house in the village!
When I'm big I'm going to be a blacksmith!
home: All I want is a roof over my head.
One day I'll have a home of my own again.
job: All I need is a steady job. That's all.
A job — any job. Then everything else will follow.
legacy: At my age you think about what you leave behind.
I want this village to outlive me. That's all I ask.
business: I'm saving for my own business. {money} so far — I need about {money2}.
One day I'll open my own shop. I've put aside {money} already.
business_ready: I've finally saved enough to open my own workshop! Now I just need the right place.
It took a long time, but the money's there. Time to start something of my own.
master: One day I'll be a master of my trade. You'll see.
I practise every day. Mastery takes time.
grow_business: I'd like to expand. More workers, more goods.
A good business never stands still.
steady: A steady job, a warm home, friends nearby. What more could I want?
I'm content. Not everyone needs to be rich.
save: I'm putting a little aside every week. {money} so far — I'd like {money2}.
No more meals out for me. Every coin goes in the tin.
buy_house: I'm tired of paying rent. I've got {money} of the {money2} a house would take.
One day this door will be mine. Saving every week for it.
better_job: I'm keeping my eyes open for better work.
This job will do for now. But only for now.
family: I'd like to meet someone. Settle down, have a family.
A home full of children — that's what I want.
settle: It's such a long walk to work. I'd like a place out there.
I'm thinking of moving closer to work. The walk is killing me.
leave: I've been thinking of leaving the valley. Nothing's holding me here.
Maybe it's time to try my luck somewhere else.
leave_packing: I'm leaving in a few days. My things are nearly packed.
This is goodbye, I think. I'm off down the west road soon.

tavern_night: It's my tavern night! Come by for a drink later.
Tonight I'll be at the tavern, same as every week.
market_today: Market day! I'm stocking up for the week.
market_tomorrow: Tomorrow I do my weekly shopping.
Market day tomorrow. Let's hope prices behave.
family_day: On my day off I visit family — {kin} will be waiting.
I'll be seeing {npc} soon. Family comes first.

fishing: After work I go fishing. The fish bite best at dusk.
Nothing beats a quiet evening by the water.
walking: I love long walks in the woods. They clear the head.
The forest paths are lovely this time of year.
reading: I've been reading in the hall. There's so much to learn.
Books are the only thing I'd spend my last coin on.
gardening: My garden is my pride. You should see my beans.
A few rows of vegetables by the house — keeps the table full.
cards: Fancy a game of cards at the tavern tonight?
I won three rounds of cards last night!
gossip: I hear everything at the well. Ask me anything!
The well is where the real news is.
whittling: I carve little figures in the evenings. Keeps my hands busy.
Whittling calms me down after a long day.
playing: Wanna play tag? Bet you can't catch me!
We found a secret spot near the plaza!
hunting: I go hunting in the woods when I can. A rabbit for the pot is worth the walk.
Stand still and the deer come right up to you. Well — almost.

fav_place: You'll usually find me at {building} in the evenings.
{building} is my favourite place in the village.

homeless: I have nowhere to live. I sleep wherever I can.
Do you know anyone renting a room? I'm desperate.
poor: I'm down to my last coins.
Money's so tight I skip meals.
lonely: I haven't had a proper talk with anyone in days.
Sometimes I feel nobody would notice if I left.
tired: I'm exhausted. I could sleep for a week.
My legs are made of lead today.
sick: I don't feel well at all.
I think I'm coming down with something.

rival: {npc}? Don't even mention that name to me.
If {npc} is there, I'm not going.
friend: {npc} is my best friend. We see each other nearly every day.
If you need a good word, ask {npc}. A wonderful person.

land: {plot} is still for sale, if you're interested.
Someone should buy {plot}. Good land going to waste.
player_biz_good: Everyone's talking about your workshop. Good furniture, fair prices.
People say you run a decent business.
player_biz_bad: People grumble about your workshop, you know. Empty shelves, high prices.
Your workshop's reputation isn't great, I'm afraid.
need_carpenter: The village could really use a carpenter. You can't find a decent chair anywhere.
If someone made furniture here, they'd do well.

good_harvest: The harvest looks rich this year. Bread will be cheap!
drought: This drought is ruining the fields. Food will get expensive.
No rain for days. The farmers are worried sick.
heavy_rain: All this rain — good for the crops, bad for my boots.
storm_front: Tie everything down — this storm is serious.
cold_snap: This cold! Firewood is worth its weight in gold now.
berry_year: The bushes are bursting with berries this year!
flood: The river flooded the low houses. What a mess.
Half the riverside is under mud.
blight: The crops are rotting in the fields. Blight, they say.
Blight again. Bread will be dear this year.
poor_harvest: The harvest is poor this year. Tighten your belt.
The farmers say it's the worst harvest in years.
sickness: Half the village is coughing. Keep warm.
There's a sickness going round — the old folk are suffering.
mine_collapse: The quarry caved in! Thank goodness nobody died.
No stone from the quarry until they make it safe.
boom: Traders are paying good money for everything we make!
Good times — the traders can't get enough of our goods.
slump: Nobody wants to buy anything. Hard times.
The traders are paying next to nothing this season.
migration_wave: Newcomers everywhere — where will they all live?
trade_fair: There's a merchant paying top price for {item}! Sell while you can.
Got any {item}? The fair merchant is buying.
bandits: Don't travel if you can help it — there are bandits on the roads.
A carter was robbed on the east road, I heard. Bandits.

student_away: {npc} is away studying in {settlement}. We get a letter now and then.
Did you hear? {npc}'s doing well at the university in {settlement}.

shortage: There's no {item} at the store again. What are we supposed to eat?
The store is out of {item}. Prices will go through the roof.
winter_wood: Winter eats firewood. I hope the woodcutters keep up.

forest_thin: We have to walk further for timber every week. The woods near the yard are getting thin.
The forest isn't what it was. Too many trees cut, too few planted.
forest_bare: There's hardly a tree left near the lumberyard. Where will our timber come from?
Stumps as far as you can see. We cut the forest down.
fish_scarce: The fish aren't biting like they used to. Too many lines in the water.
Hardly a fish left in the river. We've taken too many.
fish_good: The river is full of fish this year!
Good fishing lately — the lake is teeming.
ore_low: The old seams are running dry. We need to find new {item}.
Every week the quarry gives less {item}. Someone should go prospecting.
game_scarce: Haven't seen a deer in weeks. The woods are too quiet.
The hunting's poor. Too many hunters, not enough forest.
replanting: They've started planting saplings near the lumberyard. Smart — our grandchildren will need timber too.

good: I'll never forget what {kin_your}, {npc}, did for me. You've a lot to live up to.
{npc} — {kin_your} — was good to me when I needed it. That was {ago}.
Your family has always been kind to me. {npc} especially.
bad: I haven't forgotten what {kin_your}, {npc}, did. I hope you're different.
{npc} — {kin_your} — did me wrong, {ago}. Let's see what kind of person you are.
Your family and I have history. Not the good kind.
retired: Is {npc} enjoying the quiet life? You've big shoes to fill.
condolence: I'm sorry about {kin_your}. {npc} was one of a kind.
The village isn't the same without {npc}. I'm so sorry.
deed_family: Your family did a lot for this valley. {deed}

kids: {npc} was a handful today! Takes after you.
The children keep me busy — I wouldn't have it any other way.
crowded: We're getting a bit cramped at home, love. We could do with more room.
If we're to grow the family, we'll need a bigger house.
love: Come home early tonight, will you?
child_young: I helped today! Well, a bit.
When I grow up I want to be just like you.
child_grown: I've been thinking about what I want to do with my life.
You taught me a lot, you know.
elder: Don't make my mistakes — make your own.
The village has changed so much since I was young.

no_home: I've nowhere to sleep. That comes first.
no_work: Without work, what else is there to think about?
content: Honestly? I'm happy with things as they are.
settled_age: At my age you know what you want.
little_savings: I've nothing put by. One bad week and that's it.
children: With children to feed you think ahead.
hard_times: After what happened, I don't want to be caught short again.
prices_high: Have you seen what bread costs now?
family_needs_home: A family needs a home of its own, not a rented room.
was_evicted: I was thrown out once. Never again.
rent_high: The rent swallows half of what I earn.
house_for_sale: There's a house for sale I could almost afford.
out_of_reach: On my pay a house is a dream, if I'm honest.
knows_trade: I know this trade better than my boss does.
opportunity: The village could do with another {biz_type}. I've done the sums.
failed_before: I tried once and lost everything. I'm wary.
unhappy_at_work: I'm not happy where I work.
close_to_mastery: I'm nearly there. A little more practice.
young: I'm young. Now's the time to learn.
boss_conflict: My boss and I don't get along. At all.
better_offer: Other places pay better, you know.
wrong_trade: I trained for other work, and it's wasted here.
business_doing_well: Business is good. Time to grow.
wants_children: We're hoping for a little one.
room_at_home: There's room at home for a cradle.
long_walk: Hours on the road every day just to get to work.
hamlet: People are building out there now. It's a real place.
owns_home_here: I'd have to sell my house here, of course.
no_prospects: Weeks without work. There's nothing for me here.
unhappy: I'm just not happy here any more.
feud: I can't live next to that one a day longer.
treated_badly: After how I was treated? Why stay?
grief: Everything here reminds me of who I lost.
lost_home: My home is gone. Maybe that's a sign.
village_slump: The village is on its knees. Everyone says so.

you_headman: Everyone's watching what you do as headman, you know.
headman: {npc} is headman now. We'll see how it goes.
Have you seen what {npc} is doing as headman?
i_am_headman: Being headman is harder than it looks.
Everyone comes to me with their troubles now.
election_soon: The election's in {n} days. Who are you voting for?
Election soon. I've made up my mind already.
saving_for: The council's putting money by for a {institution}. About time.
They say we'll have a {institution} before long.

old_school: My grandmother learned her letters at {building}, same as me.
{building}'s been teaching children longer than I've been alive.
famous_institute: People come from the towns to see {building}. Imagine!
They say {building} has worked out things even the towns didn't know.
historic_workshop: Half the good craftsmen in the valley learned at {building}.
If you want to learn a trade properly, {building}'s the place.

specialty: The valley's making a name for its {field}, you know.
Folk in the towns say if you want {field} done right, you come here.
