char_hint.old: Some of the valley's oldest houses stand here.
char_hint.new: Most of what's here has only just gone up — or is going up now.
char_hint.university: Learning is what this part of the village lives by.
char_hint.none: What's built here gives this part of the village its character.

rumor.leaving: {npc} has left the village — and folks say more will follow.
rumor.new_business: {npc} has opened a new place — {building}. Worth a look, they say.
rumor.extra_rich: A whole mountain of it, apparently.
rumor.settlement_boom: they say there's plenty of {item} in {settlement} and it's going cheap
rumor.settlement_shortage: they say {settlement} is short of {item} and paying well
rumor.you_built: They say you've put up a {building_type}. Busy, aren't you!
rumor.you_helped: I heard you helped {npc}. Good of you.
rumor.you_fired: They say you let {npc} go. Hard times for them.
rumor.you_business: You've got {building} now, they say. Moving up in the world!
rumor.you_ambition: People say you've become a real {ambition}.
rumor.you_path: Word is you're on your way — {milestone}!
rumor.you_generous: You gave {money} towards {festival}, didn't you? People noticed.
rumor.copied: {npc} has started a {biz_type} — going after your trade, some say.

lineage.title: The torch passes

old_died.m: {name} has died, aged {n}. He is buried in the village graveyard, and his name is in the history book.
old_died.f: {name} has died, aged {n}. She is buried in the village graveyard, and her name is in the history book.

old_retired.m: {name} has retired at {n}. He'll spend his old age at home — you can still visit him.
old_retired.f: {name} has retired at {n}. She'll spend her old age at home — you can still visit her.

lineage.heir: You now play as {name}, aged {n} — generation {g}. The family's money, land, homes, businesses and workers are yours.
lineage.newcomer: There was no one to carry the family on. You now play as {name}, a newcomer aged {n}, starting afresh.
lineage.heir_hint: You learned something of your parent's trade at home, and the village remembers your family — for better or worse.
lineage.newcomer_hint: Nobody here knows you yet. The history of the family before you lives on in the village's history book.
lineage.single_hint: Single. Grow close to someone and you can ask them to walk out with you.
lineage.retire: Retire and hand over to your heir

retire_confirm.m: Retire? You'll continue as your son {name}. You'll stay in the village as a retired elder.
retire_confirm.f: Retire? You'll continue as your daughter {name}. You'll stay in the village as a retired elder.

lineage.retire_later: You can retire from age {n}, once your eldest is at least 16.
lineage.no_heir: You have no children to carry on the family.

region_desc.old_forest: Ancient woods west of the valley. Deer, tall timber, wild berries — and, some say, an old hermit's hut.
region_desc.north_pass: A cold road over the mountains. Miners talk of iron in the rocks up there.
region_desc.iron_hills: Bare, rust-coloured hills to the east. Coal seams show in the gullies.
region_desc.lake_country: Wide lakes and fishing hamlets to the south. People there might be looking for a new home.
region_desc.old_fort: The ruins of a fort from before anyone's grandparents' time. Old coin, old books — and old dangers.
region_desc.market_town: A busy town beyond the lakes. Its merchants could become your village's trading partners.
region_desc.far_coast: Many days away, where the land meets the sea. Few from the valley have ever seen it.

expedition.title: Beyond the valley
expedition.companions_hint: Friends may come along for {money} a day each. More people find more — and are safer on the road.
expedition.no_companions: No friends free to come along. Get to know people first.
expedition.away_hint: While you're away the village carries on without you.
expedition.back: You're back from {region_name} after {n} days on the road.
expedition.found_nothing: You found nothing of note this time.
expedition.quiet: A quiet few days — nothing much happened.
expedition.revealed: You learned the way to a new place: {region}.

found.deposit: A seam of ore — you marked a path to it from the valley's mountains
found.ruins: Old ruins: a little coin, and things worth learning
found.partner: Merchants who want to trade with your village — better prices for everything the village sells
found.settlers: Families who liked what they heard about your village. They'll come in a few days.

loss.injured: You were hurt on the road.

tech.none_yet: Nothing new yet — people are still getting by the old ways.
tech.hint: New know-how comes from the people doing the work, from reading and schooling, and from what explorers bring home.

handcart.name: Handcarts
handcart.desc: Carpenters worked out a cart one person can push. Goods travel faster and cheaper.

better_tools.name: Better tools
better_tools.desc: Sharper axes and harder picks from the smithy: more from every tree and rock.

crop_rotation.name: Crop rotation
crop_rotation.desc: Farmers rest their fields in turn. Harvests are richer.

masonry.name: Masonry
masonry.desc: Builders learned to dress stone properly. Everything is built faster.

herbal_medicine.name: Herbal medicine
herbal_medicine.desc: Gardeners learned which herbs heal. Sickness spreads less.

draft_animals.name: Draft animals
draft_animals.desc: Horses in harness: carts haul more, and fields are ploughed faster.

writing.name: Writing
writing.desc: With a school, the village writes things down. People learn faster.

wagons.name: Wagons
wagons.desc: Big iron-shod wagons carry whole loads at once.

milling.name: Milling
milling.desc: The know-how to build a water mill — the village can raise one.

printing.name: Printing
printing.desc: A printed gazette: news travels true, and people keep learning.

boats.name: Boats
boats.desc: Boats on the lake and the sea: journeys to places on the water take much less time.

irrigation.name: Irrigation
irrigation.desc: Ditches carry water to the fields. Bigger harvests.

stone_bridges.name: Stone bridges
stone_bridges.desc: Proper stone bridges and roadbeds: building goes quicker, and roads to other places cost less.

bookkeeping.name: Bookkeeping
bookkeeping.desc: Proper accounts. Traders pay a little more, and a bank becomes possible.

improved_plough.name: Improved plough
improved_plough.desc: An iron-shod plough worked out at the institute: it turns the soil deeper with less effort. Bigger harvests.

seed_selection.name: Seed selection
seed_selection.desc: Keeping the seed of the best plants, year after year. The fields yield more.

lime_mortar.name: Lime mortar
lime_mortar.desc: A stronger mortar, properly mixed and burnt. Walls go up faster and stand longer.

field_medicine.name: Field medicine
field_medicine.desc: Cleaning wounds, treating fevers, knowing what to do. Fewer fall sick, and fewer die of it.

surveying.name: Surveying
surveying.desc: Measuring the land properly. Roads cost less to lay, and building goes a little faster.

water_wheel.name: Water wheel
water_wheel.desc: Harnessing the river to turn machinery. The mill and the yards get more done.

blast_furnace.name: Blast furnace
blast_furnace.desc: A hotter furnace, driven by bellows: better iron, and more of it.

brickmaking.name: Brickmaking
brickmaking.desc: Clay from the riverbank, fired in a kiln: bricks made here instead of brought in. Someone can open a brickworks.

sawing.name: The sawmill
sawing.desc: Sawing planks in bulk instead of one at a time by hand. Someone can open a sawmill.

manufacture.name: Manufacture
manufacture.desc: Many hands, each doing one part: tools and furniture made by the dozen. The valley can have its first factory.

steam_engine.name: The steam engine
steam_engine.desc: Fire and water driving wheels: the works turn out more, and one day engines will pull trains.

railways.name: Railways
railways.desc: Iron rails and steam engines: build a station and you can lay a railway to the towns you trade with.

contract.craft: {npc} wants {qty} × {item} made — {quality} or better — delivered to their home.
contract.craft_biz: {building} needs {qty} × {item} for its workers — {quality} or better.
contract.build: {npc} is building a {vbuilding}: put in {hours} hours of work on the site.
contract.build_village: The village is building a {vbuilding}: put in {hours} hours of work on the site.
contract.hint: Contracts come from real needs around the village — and the people who need the work ask you themselves when you talk to them. Do the work yourself, or be the manager: put your workers on any contract (and on jobs from the Jobs tab — "Send my workers"). You're paid; they get their usual wage. Missing a deadline costs you reputation.
contract.none: Nothing on offer right now — check back tomorrow.
contract.order_feast: {npc} is throwing a celebration and orders {qty} × {item} from your {building2}.
contract.order_feast_village: The village is holding a feast and orders {qty} × {item} from your {building2}.
contract.harvest: {npc}'s fields are full of ripe wheat: bring in {qty} plants and take the wheat to {building}.
contract.repair: {building} is in a bad way ({n}% sound). {npc} wants it put right: {qty} points of repair work.
contract.repair_village: {building} is in a bad way ({n}% sound). The village wants it put right: {qty} points of repair work.
contract.owed: You're carrying {qty} × {item} of theirs — hand it over at {building}.
contract.no_workers: You have no workers yet — hire someone first.
contract.rank_line: {done} contracts seen through · up to {n} at once
contract.send_workers_tip: You take the job and your workers do it. You're paid; they get their usual wage.
contract.need_goods: Your workers can't get {item}: nobody sells it and it can't be gathered — put some in your storage.
contract.need_stock: {building} has no {item} in stock to send — your workers are waiting for it.
contract.job_needs_workers: No one's on this job yet — press "Manage workers" and pick who does it.

how.supply: Your workers take the goods from your storage — or buy them with your money (within the daily limit), or gather wood, stone and berries — and carry them over.
how.craft: Your workers take pieces good enough from your storage (or buy plain ones if that's all it needs) and deliver them.
how.order: A worker goes to your business and sends the goods off by cart.
how.shift: Your workers go to the employer and work the hours there.
how.deliver: Your workers take the goods from your storage, buy them, or gather them, and bring them to the employer.
how.courier: A worker picks up the parcel and takes it to the house.
how.rounds: A worker picks up the letters and takes one to each house.
how.haul: Your workers take the materials from the supplier's yard to the building site.

contract.water: {npc}'s wheat is drying out: water {qty} plants in the fields by {building}.
contract.gather: {building} is short of its own {item}: gather {qty} and bring it in.
contract.build_new: {npc} wants a new {vbuilding} built — the whole building, from the ground up.
contract.build_works: {npc} wants {building} improved: {hours} hours of building work.
contract.accept_client: Take it on — they buy the materials
contract.accept_included: Take it on — materials with their money ({money})
contract.accept_player: Take it on — I bring the materials ({money} back)
contract.at_risk: At risk: not enough hands on it to finish by the deadline.

mode.included: you buy them with the client's advance
mode.player: you get them, paid back at the end

contract.rank_next2: next: {rank} at {n} jobs and a name of {rep}
contract.found_tip: A firm with a name: one more contract at once, a crew that works a little better, businesses trust it more.

ambition.title: Ambitions
ambition.none: No ambitions chosen. Pick what you'd like to achieve — or just live.

master_craftsman.name: Master craftsman
master_craftsman.desc: Reach the top level in carpentry, smithing or cooking.

landowner.name: Landowner
landowner.desc: Own ten properties and plots of land.

big_farm.name: A big farm
big_farm.desc: Work forty fields of your own.

builder.name: Builder
builder.desc: Finish eight buildings of your own.

employer.name: Employer
employer.desc: Have five people working for you at once.

explorer.name: Explorer
explorer.desc: Learn the way to every region beyond the valley.

cartographer.name: Cartographer
cartographer.desc: Walk and map 90% of the valley.

polymath.name: Jack of all trades
polymath.desc: Reach level 5 in six different skills.

axe_care.name: Axe care
axe_care.desc: Half the wear on your axes; chop a little faster.

timber_merchant.name: Timber merchant
timber_merchant.desc: Sell wood for 25% more and planks for 15% more.

prospector.name: Prospector
prospector.desc: +1 ore or stone from every rock.

geologist.name: Geologist
geologist.desc: Now and then you spot a new seam near where you mine.

pick_care.name: Pick care
pick_care.desc: Half the wear on your pickaxes; mine a little faster.

efficient_farmer.name: Efficient farmer
efficient_farmer.desc: 30% of the time, planting doesn't use up the seed.

water_saver.name: Water saver
water_saver.desc: Your watering can holds twice as much.

net_caster.name: Net caster
net_caster.desc: A catch sometimes brings in two fish.

skinner.name: Skinner
skinner.desc: +1 hide from every animal you bring down.

fine_joinery.name: Fine joinery
fine_joinery.desc: Your furniture and woodwork come out finer.

thrifty_carpenter.name: Thrifty carpenter
thrifty_carpenter.desc: A quarter of the time you save a piece of material.

master_carpenter.name: Master carpenter
master_carpenter.desc: Masterwork furniture even before full mastery, and finer work.

toolsmith.name: Toolsmith
toolsmith.desc: The tools you forge come out finer.

smelter.name: Smelter
smelter.desc: Smelting sometimes yields an extra ingot.

chef.name: Chef
chef.desc: Your cooking comes out much finer — even masterwork.

architect.name: Architect
architect.desc: Build a little faster with a little less material; larger designs later.

market_analyst.name: Market analyst
market_analyst.desc: See which shop pays best for each thing you carry; sell a bit higher.

motivator.name: Motivator
motivator.desc: Your workers are happier working for you.

cartographer.name: Cartographer
cartographer.desc: Each expedition maps 50% more of a region.

treasure_hunter.name: Treasure hunter
treasure_hunter.desc: Every expedition turns up one more find.

biz.hint: Cheaper prices bring more customers; better wages keep good workers. A manager keeps it running well while you're elsewhere — or work a shift there yourself.
biz.no_staff: Nobody works here yet. People looking for work will come and ask.
biz.no_orders: No orders at the moment — other businesses post them on the notice board.
biz.you_have_stake: You have a stake in this business: a share of each week's profit comes to you.
biz.you_lent: They still owe you {money}, paid back weekly from profits.
biz.dealings_hint: Buy it outright, take a stake in its profits, or lend it money (paid back with interest).
biz.open_hint: The price covers fitting out and the first stock. Staff will come looking for work.
biz.short: Out of {item}: no {item2} being made ({n} days). Suppliers are being looked for — or bring some yourself.
biz.caravan_out: A caravan is on its way to {settlement} (arrives in {n} d).
biz.caravan_back: A caravan is on its way back from {settlement} ({n} d).
biz.route_no_contacts: The valley doesn't trade with any other settlement yet.
biz.route_hint: Once a week a caravan sets out (if there's something worth taking). Better carts from a carters' yard carry more.
biz.send_hint: Send one of your hired workers to work here: they join the staff and do the work, on this business's wages. You can call them back any time.

cave.name: Cave
cave.desc: A dark opening at the foot of the rocks. Cold air breathes out of it — and there's a glint of something deeper in.

mineshaft.name: Old mine shaft
mineshaft.desc: A timber frame over a shaft someone dug long ago. They must have been after something.

ruin.name: Ruins
ruin.desc: The tumbled walls of a homestead nobody remembers. Moss, stones — and maybe what the owners left behind.

cabin.name: Abandoned cabin
cabin.desc: A trapper's cabin deep in the woods, door nailed shut, roof falling in.

stones.name: Standing stones
stones.desc: Four weathered stones in a ring, older than anyone's stories. Marks are cut into them.

waystation.name: Old waystation
waystation.desc: A derelict inn on the old road out of the valley, where travellers once changed horses.

site.hire_hint: Put money down and the builders' firms ({n}) and people looking for work ({n2}) come and work on it by the hour — and buy the materials, if you tick that. What's left comes back to you when it's done.
site.points: Places to work: {a} of {b} taken · material drop: {c} of {d}

site_ui.vein: Signs of ore nearby — a seam worth mining.
site_ui.knowledge: Things worth knowing (the village's knowledge grows).
site_ui.hurt: You got hurt scrambling about in there.
site_ui.nothing: Nothing of value — but now you know.
site_ui.building: Your outpost is being built. Bring materials and work on it (or have workers do it).

goal_why.family_needs_home: a family needs a home of its own
goal_why.was_evicted: was thrown out of a rented home once
goal_why.house_for_sale: there's a house for sale they could afford
goal_why.out_of_reach: a house is out of reach on their pay
goal_why.failed_before: a business of theirs failed before
goal_why.long_walk: a long walk to work every day
goal_why.owns_home_here: owns their home in the village
goal_why.village_slump: the village is going through a slump

settlement_desc.woodhollow: Woodcutters and trappers in a clearing of the Old Forest. Timber and game aplenty; bread and iron are dear.
settlement_desc.pass_hold: A handful of herders' farms under the north pass. Cheese and hides; they have to buy in their grain.
settlement_desc.lakeside: A fishing village on the big lake. Fish, cabbages and potatoes — short of timber for boats and houses.
settlement_desc.ironford: A mining town in the iron hills. Ore, coal and iron; the miners need feeding, and their picks wear out.
settlement_desc.market_town: A real town, with a market every day. Bricks and good tools; it eats grain, timber and fine furniture.
settlement_desc.saltmere: A port on the far coast, where ships put in. Fish in plenty; it buys planks, iron and anything precious.

journey.title: Trade journey
journey.none_known: You don't know of anywhere to go yet. Explore beyond the valley (or listen to travellers) to hear of other places.
journey.road_best: The road there is as good as it gets.
journey.road_hint: A better road makes every journey there shorter and safer — for you, the village's caravans and travellers. It takes a few weeks to build.
journey.nothing_to_take: You have nothing to take. Goods in your pockets and your storage chest can be loaded.
journey.away_hint: The valley carries on while you're away. At the other end, time stands still while you trade.
journey.robbed_money: Bandits on the road took {money} from your purse.
journey.shock_boom: Plenty of {item} here this season — it's going cheap.
journey.shock_shortage: They're short of {item} — it fetches a lot right now.
journey.market_hint: Every sale lowers their price a little, every purchase raises it. What you don't sell comes home with you.
journey.stored_hint: What you brought back is in your storage chest.
journey.university_closed: Nothing you could study here yet — you need more schooling first.
journey.university_hint: A week of lectures. After enough weeks — and knowing enough — you take a degree.
journey.road_3: a stone highway with proper bridges
journey.rail_underway: The railway is being laid ({n} days to go).
journey.rail_best: There's a railway: the train takes you (and a goods wagon carries 400).
journey.rail_hint: A railway from the station: the journey takes a fraction of the time, it's almost safe, and a goods wagon carries far more than any cart. It takes a little longer to lay than a road.

map.settlements_hint: Trade journeys and caravans leave from the waymark on the west road. 🤝 = trading with the valley.
map.click_hint: Click a building on the map to see it.
map.click_hint_land: Click a building to see it, or a piece of land to look at it.
map.click_hint_places: Click a neighbourhood or a district to see what it's like.
map.click_hint_pick: Click a marker or a building to pick it — then follow, show or manage it.

market.name: Market
market.desc: A market hall and a weekly market. Traders bring news of prices in every settlement the valley trades with; exports fetch more.

watch.name: Night watch
watch.desc: Watchmen catch fires before they start and patrol the roads out of the valley.

clinic.name: Healer's house
clinic.desc: A place for the sick to be cared for. Much less sickness in the village.

guild.name: Craft guild
guild.desc: The masters teach and set standards. Everyone learns their trade faster.

bank.name: Savings bank
bank.desc: Lends to villagers starting a business, and pays you interest on your savings.

hall.title: Village affairs
hall.top_status: The valley's settlement is as great as it gets.
hall.election_hint: Everyone grown-up votes once a year — for the person they think best of, and for what they'd do: the hard-up for generous poor relief, business owners for low taxes.
hall.headman_hint: You're headman: set the taxes and poor relief, and choose what the village saves for next. People will remember at the next election.
hall.policy_hint: The headman sets the taxes and poor relief, and chooses what the village saves for.
hall.wanted: wanted — the village is saving for it
hall.bank_hint: Savings earn a little interest every week (and the bank lends them on to villagers).
hall.no_deeds: Nothing yet. Build, found, lead — the valley remembers.
hall.legacy_hint: Renown outlives you: your heir starts out trusted, and people bring up what the family did.
hall.learned_hint: The valley's brightest can study at the universities in the towns. Graduates may come home to serve as doctor, engineer or researcher, paid from the village fund — or make their lives in the town.
hall.could_study_hint: Young people who'd go to university if someone paid:

deed.outpost_founded: {name} founded an outpost: a {building_type} by the {site}.
deed.hamlet_founded: The houses round {name}'s outpost grew into {hamlet}.
deed.player_kept_villager: {name} talked {npc} into staying in the valley.
deed.player_benefactor: {name} gave a building back to the village.

affairs.title: Your affairs
affairs.transfers_hint: Money put in or taken out of the bank or your businesses' tills, borrowed or repaid, or inherited — not earned or spent.
affairs.upkeep_week: Feed for your animals, per week
affairs.no_goods: You own nothing but the clothes on your back.
affairs.no_props_text: Build a house on land of your own, or buy an empty one in the village — then let it and collect rent.

ledger.donations: Roads and gifts to the village

letting.title: Tenants
letting.not_fit: Nobody will rent it as it is — it needs repairs first (or it's not empty).
letting.interested: Might take it at this rent
letting.viewing_today: {npc} is coming to look at it this evening.
letting.advertised_until: Advertised in the village for {n} more days.
letting.ad_out: Notice posted in {settlement} — answers in about {n} days.
letting.hint: With the sign up, villagers who could use a better home come to look at it in the evening. Advertising reaches people who aren't even looking. A notice in another town can bring a family from there. Cheaper rent means more takers.
letting.hint_no_contacts: With the sign up, villagers who could use a better home come to look at it in the evening. Advertising reaches people who aren't even looking. Once the valley trades with other towns, you can advertise there too.

letting_why.own_place: wants a place of their own

learn.talented: The teacher thinks this one has a real gift.
learn.player_hint: Learn at the school's evening class or on a trade-school course, from a tutor (ask someone learned), beside a master (ask to be their apprentice), at the library, or at a university on your travels. What you study makes the matching skill come faster.

kind_desc.school: The village school: the little ones learn their letters and sums here, and — with a learned enough teacher — older pupils go further.
kind_desc.grammar: An upper school: mathematics, natural science, history and geography, a little economics and building — for youngsters who have finished primary school.
kind_desc.trade: A trade school: a year's course in a trade — building, carpentry, smithing, mechanics, farming, cooking, trade or mining — taught by someone who's mastered it. Youngsters come by day; grown-ups starting over, in the evenings.

school.head: Head teacher
school.class_closed: Not running — no teacher here knows enough to teach it.

q_tip.teacher: What the teacher knows of the subjects, and how well they get it across (years of teaching help).
q_tip.building: The school's repair: {n}%. A leaking roof and a cold room make for poor lessons.
q_tip.crowd: Pupils per seat. A crowded room teaches everyone less.
q_tip.ratio: Pupils per teacher. One teacher can only teach so many.
q_tip.books: Books and slates: {n} for everyone. The village buys more each week (more if the schooling policy is generous; half price once printing is known).

school.q_mentor: An experienced teacher here helps the others along.
school.hint: Lessons are only as good as the room they're given in: a teacher who knows their subjects and how to teach, a building in repair, seats and books enough. The village pays the teachers and buys books from its fund; the headman's schooling policy decides how generously.
school.no_teacher_long: The school has no teacher: no lessons until someone takes the post.
school.teachers_hint: Teachers grow better with the years: junior, teacher, senior, master. The best teacher heads the school, and experienced teachers help the others along. Unpaid teachers leave.
school.need_instructor: an instructor competent at a trade ({n}+)
school.course_subjects: Mostly the trade itself, with the arithmetic and reading it needs. Courses: {list}.
school.course_hint: Trade courses are held on Tuesday and Thursday evenings: come to the trade school then. Enough lessons, knowing enough of the trade, and you're qualified.
school.endow: Pay the teachers for a month ({money})
school.endowment_left: Your gift still covers {money} of the teachers' pay.

institute.desc: A place where the learned work on new know-how. One project at a time; it needs researchers who know enough, instruments, and money every week. Whether it works depends on how good all of that really is.
institute.unfunded: The village hasn't paid for {n} week(s): the work is stalling.
institute.choosing: Deciding what to work on next: {list}.
institute.nothing_to_do: Nothing the valley could work on yet — more know-how has to come first.
institute.no_researchers: No researchers: nobody to do the work.
institute.none: Nobody yet. A researcher needs to know natural science ({n}+) — a university graduate, usually.
institute.hint: A success becomes the valley's know-how for good, and makes a name for whoever led it. A partial result keeps some of the work; a failure, less. Better-trained researchers, full instruments and steady money make success likelier.
institute.endowment_left: Your gift still covers {money} of the work.
institute.you_choose: You've given to the institute: you may choose what it works on next.

edu_stats.title: Learning in the valley
edu_stats.hint: Counted from the people themselves: schooling among grown-ups, reading among everyone from eight.

structure.none: This is not a building that can be improved.
structure.quality_hint: Quality is how well it was built and kept: materials, the builder's skill, rooms and renovations. At this level it can be up to {n}%.
structure.owner_decides: Only the owner decides what's done to it.
structure.nothing_more: There's nothing more to do to it for now.
structure.works_hint: The money is paid now; the materials must be brought to the site and the hours put in — by you, your workers or hired builders. The building stays in use while the work goes on.

works_fx.wider: {n} tile(s) wider — needs free ground beside it
works_fx.not_a_home: nobody can live in it any more
works_fx.one_building: {building} becomes part of it — one building
works_fx.ground_freed: the ground is free to build on again

bedroom.name: Bedroom
bedroom.desc: Another bedroom: room for two more people.

kitchen.name: Kitchen
kitchen.desc: A proper kitchen with a range. More comfortable, and tenants like it.

cellar.name: Cellar
cellar.desc: A stone cellar: more storage, and it keeps the worst of the winter frost out.

pantry.name: Pantry
pantry.desc: Shelves and a cool corner for food and things.

parlour.name: Parlour
parlour.desc: A room for sitting and receiving guests. Comfort, and a better name for the house.

washroom.name: Washroom
washroom.desc: A room for washing, with water carried or piped from the well. Healthier and more pleasant.

upper_floor.name: Upper floor
upper_floor.desc: A second storey on top: room for three more people.

cart_shed.name: Cart shed
cart_shed.desc: A lean-to beside the house for a cart or a handcart. Takes a tile of ground beside it.

garden.name: Garden
garden.desc: A fenced garden beside the house: vegetables, flowers, a fruit tree. Takes two tiles of ground.

extra_bench.name: Extra workbench
extra_bench.desc: Another bench and tools: one more person can work here.

tool_racks.name: Tool racks
tool_racks.desc: Everything in its place: a little more gets done.

storeroom.name: Storeroom
storeroom.desc: More room for stock and supplies.

yard_shed.name: Yard shed
yard_shed.desc: A shed in the yard for timber, stone or goods. Takes a tile of ground beside it.

barn.name: Barn
barn.desc: A big barn for hay, grain and tools. Takes two tiles of ground beside it.

display.name: Display window
display.desc: A glazed window with the goods on show. Draws customers in.

stockroom.name: Stockroom
stockroom.desc: A back room for stock: the shelves can be kept fuller.

loading_bay.name: Loading bay
loading_bay.desc: A covered bay for carts to load and unload: more stock, one more hand. Takes a tile of ground.

library_room.name: Library room
library_room.desc: A room of books for the pupils.

shop_floor.name: Shop on the ground floor
shop_floor.desc: The ground floor made into business premises.

courtyard.name: Courtyard
courtyard.desc: A paved yard with a tree for the residents. Takes a tile of ground.

lift.name: Goods lift
lift.desc: A hoist to lift loads to the upper floors.

family.name: Family home
family.desc: Arranged for one family to live well.

boarding.name: Boarding house
boarding.desc: Rooms let separately: more people, cheaper rent, a little shabbier.

luxury.name: Fine residence
luxury.desc: Furnished and kept to a high standard: higher rent from those who can pay.

workers.name: Workers' housing
workers.desc: Plain flats for working families: more people, lower rents.

bargain.name: Bargain shop
bargain.desc: Draws those who count every coin.

bhist.no_works: Nothing has been done to it yet.

tool_use.pickaxe: Breaks rock for stone, coal and ore.
tool_use.watering_can: Waters crops (refill at a well or the river).
tool_use.fishing_rod: Fishing in the river and the lake.

station_where.forge: Made at a forge: the smithy lets you use theirs for a fee, or build your own.
station_where.workbench: Made at the workbench in your home.
station_where.stove: Made at the stove in your home.

works_req.time: ≈ {n} h of work (about {d} days for one builder)
works_req.all_delivered: All the materials are on site.
works_req.change_hint: Not everything can become everything: a house can be a shop or a workshop, a workshop a warehouse… Joining needs a building of yours of the same kind close beside it, the ground between them free. Pulling down takes time too — and what's salvaged is yours.

rent_ui.title: Rent
rent_ui.range: Going rate for homes this size
rent_ui.from_next_week: The tenants pay {money} until the next rent day.
rent_ui.hint: Set exactly what you ask. Tenants already living there pay the new rent from the next rent day — raise it too far and they'll give notice.

wtask.cfetch: Taking {item} from your storage for a job
wtask.corder: Sending an order off by cart

workers.buy_hint: Workers may buy what a site of yours is missing, with your money, up to a daily limit ({money} left today).
workers.contract_prio_medium: Contracts before most of their usual work.
workers.contract_prio_low: Their usual work first; contracts when there's time.
workers.manager_tip: They stop doing the work themselves and run the rest: go round the jobs, put the best-suited workers on each contract, take them off jobs that are stuck, give roles, keep notes. Paid more.
workers.no_manager: Tip: make one of your workers manager, and they'll put the others on your contracts for you (you can still choose yourself).
workers.manager_sub: Goes round your jobs and decides who works where. A crew or a role you choose yourself is left as you set it.
workers.post_tip: They join the staff there and do its work, paid from its till. You can call them back any time.
workers.posted_at: at {building} · {money} a day from the till
workers.equipment_hint: You have {n} pieces. Lend a barrow or cart to a worker and they carry four times as much a trip.
workers.equipment_none: Buy or make a barrow or basket, and lend it to a worker: they'll carry far more a trip.
workers.orders_none: Carrying you set up once: "60 wood a day to my warehouse", "keep 50 planks in store".

land_ui.gone: This land isn't there as it was any more.
land_ui.buy_hint: You buy land standing on it (or right beside it). Land that belongs to nobody is bought from the village — it keeps the register.
land_ui.chip_tip: The land you're standing on. Click to look at it — and to buy it.
land_ui.calls_housing: homes for the {n} who work nearby
land_ui.calls_shop: a shop for the {n} houses around
land_ui.calls_quiet: less noise — workshops sit close to houses
land_ui.next_door_hint: Walk over to a plot to buy it and grow your holding.
land_ui.infra_unlinked: the road doesn't link up to the village
land_ui.reshape_hint: Join plots of yours that lie side by side into one — or split one in two, to sell half or build on half.

lease.title: Tenancy
lease.leaving: {npc} has given notice: they leave in {n} days ({letting}).
lease.notice_out: {npc} has been given notice: they leave in {n} days.
lease.confirm: Give them notice? They'll have {n} days to leave, and people will think a little less of you.
lease.confirm_cause: Give them notice for the rent they owe? They'll have {n} days to leave.

manager.none_hint: no manager yet — ask someone who knows you well

housing_why.better_home: a home that suits them better

market_ui.title: Housing market
market_ui.no_data: The market's first figures come at the end of the week.
market_ui.hint: When more people are looking than there are homes free, rents and prices climb — and building houses to let begins to pay.

territory_why.mining: stone in the ground (or a cave near)
territory_why.education: a school or a place of learning
territory_why.mixed: homes, trade and work side by side

land_event.split: Split in two: {plot} is the other half.

place_ui.faded: This neighbourhood no longer holds together — too few are left living there.
place_ui.gone: This part of the village has changed beyond recognition.
place_ui.standing_hint: Kept houses, a shop, a well and quiet streets make a place people want to live — its houses fetch more, and villagers choosing a home rate it higher.

hood_event.founded: The houses here grew into a neighbourhood.
hood_event.founded_old: One of the valley's first neighbourhoods.
hood_event.decline: People are leaving: {n} still live here.

district_event.formed: This part of the village took shape ({to}).
district_event.formed_old: Part of the village from its first days ({to}).

infra_ui.summary: Road tiles {roads} · cobbled {paved} · bridges {bridges} · lamps {lamps} · homes on the road network {linked} / {homes}
infra_ui.nothing_yet: The village hasn't built any roads or lamps of its own yet.
infra_ui.works_hint: A share of the taxes goes into the fund. Each week the village spends it on what's most needed: a lane to a house cut off from the roads, cobbles on the busiest street (once it's a large village, or knows masonry), a lamp for a neighbourhood left in the dark.

dev_plan.home: {npc} bought it to build a home on.
dev_plan.hold: {npc} is holding it while land grows dearer.
dev_plan.develop: {npc} is building a row of houses here.

dev_ui.none: Nobody is buying land to build on just now.
dev_ui.row: {npc}: a row of houses to let ({built} of {n} built)
dev_ui.lot: {npc}: a lot for a home of their own

flats.title: Flats
flats.summary: {let} of {units} let · up to {cap} people each
flats.shop_floor_rent: let to a trader: {money} a week
flats.hint: Each flat has its own tenancy: its own rent, its own notice. The sign stays up while a flat is free. Rooms added to the building — a courtyard, a washroom, a lift — are for everyone in it.

manager_note.moved: Moved {npc} to the {ckind} job — it's at risk.
manager_note.pulled_stuck: Took everyone off the {ckind} job — they can't get on with it.
manager_note.pulled_idle: Took everyone off the {ckind} job — nothing's been done for hours.

equip.title: Your equipment
equip.lend_to_hint: Pick something for {name} to use. If it's standing somewhere, they'll walk over and fetch it when they're next at work.
equip.has_already: {npc} already has your {eq} — lending something else takes that back first.
equip.none_hint: Buy a basket at the store, a wheelbarrow at the smithy or carpenter's, or make one at your workbench. It helps whoever carries goods: you or your workers.
equip.hint: Equipment is real: it stands where it was left. A worker you lend it to walks over, takes it, and carries far more per trip. Take it back at any time — they'll bring it to your yard.
equip.retrieve_tip: They finish what they're carrying, bring it to your yard and leave it there.
equip.repair_tip: Out of use for about {hours} h, then as good as new.
equip.upgrade_tip: Better made: holds 20% more and wears slower.
equip.shop_line: Holds {cap} (by hand 20 — ×{x}) · {road}% on roads, {off}% over grass
equip.shop_hint: A basket comes straight into your hands; anything bigger is left for you in front of the shop — walk over and take it, or lend it to a worker.
equip.desc_hand: Carried by hand: a little more per trip, no slower.
equip.desc_push: Pushed on wheels: much more per trip; quick on roads, slower over grass.
equip.desc_pull: A big wagon, drawn by hand: a lot per trip, but slow — best on roads.
equip.desc_animal: An animal does the pulling: quick and strong — but it needs feeding.
equip.desc_vehicle: An engine does the work (not yet in this age).
equip.made_desc: Holds {n} a trip. It'll stand beside you when it's made.
equip.bay_hint: The repair bay mends equipment twice as fast.
equip.no_bay_hint: Build the depot up to level 2 for a repair bay (repairs twice as fast).
equip.where_away: On the road with a caravan
equip.expected_more: Carries {x}× as much a trip — fewer trips, faster work.
equip.expected_same: No more than they carry now.
equip.goes_to_fetch: {name} will fetch it on the way to the next task.

sheet.road_linked: On a road to the square
sheet.road_near: A road {n} tiles away (not linked up)

guide.all_good: All's well — carry on as you like.
guide.paths_hint: Pick a path to follow: a career, milestone by milestone, with rewards along the way. You can change it any time.
guide.show_hud: Show the guide in the corner
guide.hide_hud: Hide the guide from the corner

first_job.name: Find your first job
first_job.hint: Read the notice board on the plaza (walk up to it, press E) and take a job. Villagers sometimes offer work when you talk to them, too.

chop_wood.name: Chop some wood
chop_wood.hint: Walk up to a tree with your axe and press E. Wood sells, and you'll need it to build.

earn_100.name: Earn your first $100
earn_100.hint: Jobs from the notice board, and selling what you gather or make at the store.

craft.name: Make something
craft.hint: At the workbench in your home: planks from wood, then tools and furniture. Better skill, better quality.

hire.name: Hire a worker
hire.hint: Talk to someone out of work and offer them a job. Your workers (key K) gather, carry and build for you.

contract.name: Finish a contract
contract.hint: Villagers ask for help — a harvest, a repair, a building. Take it on, put your workers on it (Journal → Tasks), get paid.

two_workers.name: A crew of two
two_workers.hint: Hire another pair of hands: two can carry and build at the same time.

buy_land.name: Buy land
buy_land.hint: Open the map (M), click a plot for sale, or walk up to a land sign and press E.

build_store.name: Build a storage shed or barn
build_store.hint: Build menu (B) → Storage. Your workers fetch from it and bring goods back to it.

build_two.name: Put up two buildings
build_two.hint: Build menu (B): a house, a workshop, a barn… Deliver the materials, then work on it (or let your workers).

get_equipment.name: Get a wheelbarrow (or a basket)
get_equipment.hint: Buy one at the smithy or the store, or make one at your workbench. It lets a worker carry four times as much.

lend_equipment.name: Lend it to a worker
lend_equipment.hint: Workers (K) → a worker's card → Equipment → Lend… They fetch it and carry far more a trip.

big_store.name: A warehouse or transport depot
big_store.hint: Build menu (B): a warehouse holds 400, a depot keeps your barrows and carts (and repairs them).

standing_order.name: Set up a standing order
standing_order.hint: Workers (K) → Standing orders: "move 60 wood a day to my warehouse", "keep 50 planks in store"… and it gets done every day.

contracts_3.name: Become a handyman
contracts_3.hint: Finish three contracts well: your name as a contractor grows, and bigger jobs come your way.

business.name: Own a business
business.hint: Buy one that's for sale, or open your own in a building of yours.

path.name: Choose your path
path.hint: Journal → Guide: pick a career to follow — contractor, transport, landlord, business, founder or craftsman.

contractor.name: Master contractor
contractor.desc: Build for others: from odd jobs to your own construction company.

transport.name: Transport company
transport.desc: Barrows, carts and wagons: move the valley's goods.

m.caravan: A caravan of your own there and back

landlord.name: Landlord
landlord.desc: Own land and houses, and let them to tenants.

business.name: Business owner
business.desc: Own businesses, staff them, and grow rich.

m.staffed: Two of your workers staffing them

founder.name: Town founder
founder.desc: Win the valley over and help it grow into a town.

m.large_village: The village grows into a large village

craftsman.name: Master craftsman
craftsman.desc: Carpentry, smithing or cooking — make the finest work in the valley.

advice.eat: You're hungry — eat something (Q) before your health suffers.
advice.health: Your health is low — rest, eat well, or see the clinic.
advice.rent: You owe {money} in rent — pay it before you're thrown out.
advice.payroll: Your workers' wages are {money} a day and you can't pay them tomorrow.
advice.idle_workers: {n} of your workers have nothing to do — give them a site, a contract or a standing order.
advice.site_waiting: A building site is waiting for {item} — none in your storage. Buy it, fetch it, or let your workers buy it.
advice.contract_risk: A contract ({ckind}) may not be finished in time — put more hands on it.
advice.offers: {n} job offers are waiting for an answer.
advice.lend: Your {eq} stands unused — lend it to a worker.
advice.repair_eq: Your {eq} is badly worn — repair it.
advice.get_equipment: Your workers carry by the armful — a wheelbarrow would let them carry four times as much.
advice.repair_building: {building} is falling apart — have it repaired.
advice.can_hire: You can hire workers now — talk to someone out of work.
advice.can_buy_land: You can buy land now — have a look at the map (M).
advice.can_build: You own land — build something on it (B).
advice.try_orders: Try a standing order: your workers keep your stores stocked every day.
advice.manager: With three workers, a manager could organise them for you.
advice.choose_path: Choose a path to follow (Journal → Guide).
advice.festival_now: It's {festival} — go to the square and join in (people will warm to you).
advice.festival_soon: Tomorrow is {festival}: the village will gather on the square.
advice.firewood: Get firewood in for winter: put wood in your home storage ({have} there now — you'll want about {n}).
advice.snow_roads: Snow on the roads: barrows and carts are slow. Clearing snow pays on the notice board.
advice.harvest_rush: The harvest rush is on: farm work pays more right now.
advice.river_up: The river's up — the clay pits are underwater for a few days, and come back full.
advice.freight_waiting: A load is waiting for you to carry ({n} in all) — see your deliveries.
advice.try_freight: You've got something to carry goods in: sign up as a carrier on the notice board and the shops will pay you to move their goods.
advice.build_station: The valley knows how to build railways: put up a railway station.
advice.lay_railway: Your station's ready: lay a railway to a town you trade with (the journey map).
advice.fodder: Winter fodder for your horses: they eat 1 a day each from your storage (wheat, cabbages, potatoes, apples) — about {n} needed, {have} there now.
advice.livestock_fodder: Winter fodder for your farm animals: about {n} for a week (you have {have}). The store sells hay.
advice.collect_produce: Your barn is nearly full of eggs, milk and wool ({building}) — collect it before it spoils.
advice.try_livestock: Your barn has room for animals: buy chickens, sheep or cows at the village farm (eggs, milk and wool every week).
advice.rival_busy: Your rival {npc} took {n} jobs from the board this week — take them sooner, or deal with them.
advice.story_waiting: 📜 {story}: {npc} is waiting to talk to you.
advice.town_meeting: Town meeting in {n} day(s) on "{proposal}" — speak for it or against it at the hall.

orders.title: Standing orders
orders.hint: Set it up once, and your workers do it every day: they walk to the source, load up (a barrow-load if they have one), carry it over and unload.
orders.none_hint: For example: move 60 wood a day from your lumberyard to your warehouse, or keep 50 planks in store.

kind_hint.move: Every day, this much is carried from one place to the other.
kind_hint.keep: Whenever there's less than this, they fetch more (from where you choose).
kind_hint.supply: Everything the site still needs is carried over, until it's built.

orders.no_sites: You have no building sites to supply.
orders.need_workers: You need workers to carry out orders.

state.no_target: The place isn't yours any more

freight.title: Carting
freight.intro: Every day the valley's shops and workshops send goods to each other. Porters (or the village carters) carry them — unless you do. You're paid when the goods arrive, and more if they're on time.
freight.self_text: Put your name down as a carrier: some loads come to you, one at a time. Pick them up at the seller's door and take them to the buyer's (press E at the door).
freight.rate_hint: Cheaper wins more work; dearer pays more a load.
freight.record: Late {late} times · given back to the porters {handed} times
freight.firm_text: With a transport depot of your own you can register a company ({money}): your workers carry deliveries too, with their barrows and carts, and you can take on several at once.
freight.firm_running: Your company runs from {building}. {n} workers carry for it (as well as their other work).
freight.none_text: Sign up as a carrier and the valley's loads start coming your way.
freight.no_jobs_text: New loads come in as the shops restock (about {share}% of them come to you).
freight.go_yourself: Go to the seller's door and press E to load it.
freight.waiting_hands: Waiting for a free pair of hands.
freight.no_contacts: Nowhere to send a caravan yet
freight.no_contacts_text: Make contact with another settlement first (a trade journey, or an expedition).
freight.need_cart: A caravan needs a cart or a wagon of yours that's free (a handcart at least).
freight.need_driver: A caravan needs one of your workers to drive it.
freight.estimate: Should fetch about {money} · {n} days there and back · risk of robbery {risk}%
freight.board_on: You're a carrier: {n} deliveries now (you get about {share}% of the loads).
freight.board_off: The shops send goods to each other every day. Sign up and some of the carrying (and the pay) comes to you.
freight.workers_none: Deliveries for the shops, and caravans to other places.

livestock.title: Your animals
livestock.intro: Chickens, sheep and cows live at your barns. Each morning they give eggs, milk or wool into the barn — collect it (or your workers will). They graze all year but winter, when they eat fodder from your storage (hay, wheat, vegetables).
livestock.no_barn_text: Build a barn on your land (Build → Storage): that's where animals live.
livestock.fodder: Fodder in your storage: {n} — enough for about {days} winter days.

station.title: Railway station
station.no_lines_text: Lay a railway to a town you trade with (the journey map) and the trains will start coming.
station.intro: Trains come in from each town on the line three times a day, wait at the platform, and go back out. Newcomers to the valley arrive by train, and travellers spend a little in the village.
station.yard_hint: Your workers fetch what's here to your storage, or collect it yourself.
station.send_line: {n} goods waiting for the train to {settlement}
station.send_sold: Sold in {settlement} for {money} — the money's on its way
station.nothing_to_send: Nothing in your storage to send
station.send_hint: The railway's carters fetch it from your storage; it goes with the next train, is sold there, and the money comes back with a later one.
station.send_estimate: Should fetch about {money} · carriage {fee} · money back in about {n} days
station.order_hint: Bought at their price, plus carriage. It arrives in the goods yard in about {n} day(s).
station.order_note: Ordered goods wait in the goods yard at the station until they're collected.

rival.title: Your rival
rival.none_text: Get on in business (level {level}, a few workers or contracts) and someone will want a share of it.
rival.stage_rival: {npc} runs a company of their own, competing with yours: taking jobs you leave on the notice board, carrying goods, buying land.
rival.stage_partner: {npc} is your business partner now: no more competing, and a share of their takings comes to you each week.
rival.stage_bought: You bought {npc} out. Their business is yours.
rival.war_text: Cut your prices for {n} days (it costs you {money}): they'll win few jobs and lose money every day. If their money runs out, they go bust and sell up.
rival.partner_text: If you're on good terms (friendship {rel}+), go into business together: they stop competing, and {n}% of their weekly takings is yours.
rival.buy_text: Their business, their land — yours. They're paid well and step aside.
rival.log_took: took a job from the board ({ckind})
rival.log_poached: took on {npc}, who used to work for you

start.text: {npc_a} is fuming. "It's {npc_b} — they've moved the fence onto my side again, and when I said so they laughed at me. You're a fair sort. Tell them!"
start.side_a: Take {npc_a}'s side: go and have words with {npc_b}.
start.side_b: Say {npc_b} is in the right — the fence was always there.
start.mediate: Bring them together and settle it fairly.

worse.text: {npc_b} stops you in the lane. "Did you hear? Someone kicked my fence down last night — and we both know who. There's damage. What are you going to do about it?"
worse.pay_repairs: Pay for the repairs yourself ($40) and get them to shake hands.
worse.headman: Take it to the headman to judge.
worse.let_be: Let them sort it out themselves.

end.peace: {npc_a} and {npc_b} shook hands over the fence — thanks to you.
end.mended: You paid for the fence, and {npc_a} and {npc_b} made it up.
end.judged: The headman ruled for {npc_b} in the fence quarrel with {npc_a}.
end.bitter: {npc_a} and {npc_b} no longer speak — a feud that will last.

start.text: {npc_elder} looks older today. "I've no one left here, you know. But my sister's child went to {settlement} years ago… I'd give a lot to see them before I go. Would you find them for me?"
start.go: Promise to find them next time you're in {settlement}.
start.write: Pay a courier to carry a letter there ($30).

search.wait: Travel to {settlement} (a trade journey) to find {npc_elder}'s family.

letter.told: A letter came back from {settlement} for {npc_elder}: the family is coming!

found.text: {npc_elder}'s eyes fill. "You found them! They're coming — to stay, they say. I don't know how to thank you… here, take this, it's not much."

end.reunited: {npc_elder}'s family came from {settlement} to live in the valley — you found them.
end.alone: {npc_elder} never heard from the family in {settlement}.

start.text: A newcomer, {npc_s}, keeps to themselves at the edge of the village. They look tired and have almost nothing. "I'll work at anything," they say quietly. "I just need a start."
start.hire: Take them on as a worker.

secret.text: {npc_s} takes you aside. "I owe you the truth. Where I come from I was a master of {trade} — until I lost everything. You helped me when no one else would. Let me repay you."
secret.keep: Tell them it was nothing — a friend is enough.

gone.told: {npc_s}, the quiet stranger, has left the valley.

end.master: {npc_s}, once a master of {trade}, taught you the craft.
end.friend: {npc_s}, the stranger, became a true friend.
end.left: {npc_s}, the stranger, moved on as quietly as they came.

story_ui.none_text: Get to know the valley. Its people have their own troubles — and sooner or later they'll come to you.
story_ui.waiting: {npc} is waiting to talk to you
story_ui.later: What happens next will come in its own time.

meeting.title: Town meeting
meeting.none_text: Every couple of weeks the valley meets at the hall to decide something. The next one will be announced a few days ahead.
meeting.not_yet: Once the valley is a large village, its people will meet at the hall to decide things together.
meeting.sway: Your word sways about {n}% of the valley (more with a better name, on the council, or as headman).

pave_square.name: Cobble the streets
pave_square.desc: Money for the public works to lay cobbles on the busiest streets — quicker walking and carting.

gas_lamps.name: Gas lamps
gas_lamps.desc: Street lamps in the neighbourhoods still in the dark.

green.name: A village green
green.desc: Lay out a green with trees and benches: the whole valley's spirits lift.

market_day.name: A weekly market day
market_day.desc: For two months, a market on the square once a week: the store and tavern do well, and people enjoy it.

school_fund.name: Money for the school
school_fund.desc: Put money aside for the school: teachers, books, a bigger classroom.

better_road.name: A better road
better_road.desc: The village pays for a better road to the town it trades with most.

history_ui.title: The valley in numbers
history_ui.too_soon: Not enough weeks yet — the record grows each week.

bcard.walk_up: Walk up to it (E) for everything you can do here.
bcard.hint: 1–9 or click · E: the first · Esc: close

ready.materials_hint: You can start: the site waits for the materials (your workers fetch them).

wcard2.walk_up: Walk up to them to talk.

wf.none_match_hint: Try another filter, or clear the search.

note.stuck_walking: {name} couldn't get where they were going — sent on to other work.
note.stuck_working: {name} was held up at work — sent on to the next task.
note.stuck_arrived: {name} got there but couldn't start — sent on to other work.
